title: Apple Watch Series 12: Three new features coming next week
snippet: Apple Watch Series 12 is coming next week, launching at the September event alongside Apple Watch Ultra 4. Here are three new features rumored for Apple Watch Series 12. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Series 12 is coming next week, launching at the September event alongside Apple Watch Ultra 4. Here are three new features rumored for Apple Watch Series 12.

#1: New S-class chip

Apple’s S-class chips don’t get meaningful updates very often. Even though Apple does change the number most years, actual CPU improvements are rare. And last year, the company skipped offering an S11 altogether and kept the S10 around.

But this year, rumors indicate an upgraded S-class chip is coming to Apple Watch Series 12. Likely named S12 or S11, it will be more powerful, faster, and also the first new Watch chip of the AI era.

Siri AI is a tentpole addition to watchOS 27, and it’s expected to run best on the new chip. But other everyday features should benefit from the new chip too.

#2: Always-on heart rate sensor and more health improvements

Apple Watch Series 12 has long been rumored to add new health features. For example, the FDA reportedly reviewed an upgrade to hypertension notifications that’s expected to debut next week.

One other specific rumor is that the heart rate sensor will get always-on support. This would match functionality offered by competing products like WHOOP.

Per Mark Gurman, the new Series 12 sensor can “continuously collect data throughout the day — not just when it senses you’re doing intense activity or at other random intervals.”

#3: Ceramic case option, likely in white and dark gray

Joining the usual new watch bands and case options, Apple is expected to debut a Ceramic case for the first time since 2019’s Series 5 model. 

Apple will reportedly offer Series 12 in two Ceramic colors: white and dark gray. Per Bloomberg: “Apple has tested both white and dark gray configurations for the Series 12 ceramic cases.”

It’s unclear how much of a premium Ceramic will add to the Series 12 price, but the last time it was offered, it started at $1,299—far more than Apple Watch Ultra costs today.

title: Judge Lets Musk Keep ‘Twitter’ for Now but Forces Him to Release the Bird
snippet: X’s continued need of “formerly Twitter” just won it a preliminary injunction.
fullText:
The social media site X, formerly known as Twitter, gets to retain the Twitter trademark for the moment, thanks to a partial preliminary injunction against Operation Bluebird, Inc.’s Twitter.new. But by the same ruling, Bluebird gets to keep the birds and tweets. Bluebird responded to this fail whale by announcing it would rename its nascent social network from Twitter.now to Tweet.app.

District Judge Colm F. Connolly said in an opinion issued Thursday that because X still uses the word “Twitter” in its branding, the company would likely prevail if the trademark dispute in the US District Court for the District of Delaware went to final adjudication. 

“X Corp.’s use of the ‘formerly known as Twitter’ parenthetical in its Apple App Store listing makes it unlikely that Bluebird will strictly prove that X Corp. discontinued its use of the Twitter-formative marks,” Connolly wrote.

In other words, X has thus far failed to dislodge Twitter from the public consciousness despite Musk’s scorched-earth approach to destroying its social capital. It’s been three years — “Twitter” should have been gone by now. As a result, the company is still using “Twitter” so we know what it’s talking about.

The ruling does allow Bluebird to continue using “Tweet” and the iconic bird logo, mostly because X didn’t produce convincing evidence that it was still using them and because a lot of the proof X offered — web pages and emails — was undated.

Operation Bluebird announced plans last year to flip Musk the bird by launching Twitter.new in reaction to what many people perceive as the decline of the platform in the wake of Musk’s acquisition and subsequent actions, like diluting account verification, ineffectively combating hate speech and more (or as the new blue site says, “burned it all down”).

In December 2025, X filed suit against Bluebird to block it from using its textual or graphic trademarks: “Twitter,” “tweet” and the bird. Bluebird’s network is still in its please-sign-up phase.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Lori Grunin
						

						

							Senior Editor / Computers and Gaming Hardware						
					

											

								

											I've been reviewing hardware and software, devising testing methodology and handing out buying advice for more than 25 years.

title: Will the iPhone 18 Pro’s biggest upgrade really deliver?
snippet: In general, we’re not expecting the iPhone 18 Pro to be a significant upgrade over its predecessor. Indeed, if you currently have an older iPhone there are arguments for buying the iPhone 17 Pro ahead of next week’s launch. Of the few upgrades we are expecting, the biggest one on paper is going to be a variable aperture lens for the primary camera. But will this make a significant difference in reality … ? more…
fullText:
In general, we’re not expecting the iPhone 18 Pro to be a significant upgrade over its predecessor. Indeed, if you currently have an older iPhone there are arguments for buying the iPhone 17 Pro ahead of next week’s launch.

Of the few upgrades we are expecting, the biggest one on paper is going to be a variable aperture lens for the primary camera. But will this make a significant difference in reality … ?

Variable aperture offers control over depth of field

One of the biggest differences in the results you can achieve with a DSLR or mirrorless camera over an iPhone photo is control over the depth of field (DOF).

With a conventional camera, a wide aperture will create a shallow DOF that is most commonly used to separate the subject of the photo from the background. Portrait shots are a classic example (and this is why Apple’s simulated shallow depth of field feature is known as Portrait mode).

Conversely, when shooting something like a landscape or cityscape, you would typically use a narrow aperture to ensure everything is in focus from foreground to background. 

A variable aperture is therefore a standard feature of any conventional camera lens. iPhones, in contrast, have fixed aperture lenses. (There are some ways to achieve shallow DOF with an iPhone, and I’ll cover these in a separate piece after the launch of the new phone, but these are exceptions rather than the rule.)

A variable aperture iPhone lens

We’re expecting this is to be the year that the iPhone gets a variable aperture lens for the first time. It’s as yet unclear whether this feature will apply to both iPhone 18 Pro models or only to the Pro Max. Either way, it’s expected to be limited to the main camera, not the wide-angle or telephoto.

On paper, this is big news. In principle, a variable aperture lens allows us to control the depth of field. In practice, we shouldn’t get overly excited about being able to achieve the effect shown in the main photo above – and that’s because of what won’t be changing.

The bad news

The main limiting factor of iPhones is not the lens aperture – which is already rather wide – but rather the size of the sensor. Again, all else being equal, the larger the sensor, the shallower DOF you’ll be able to achieve. Compared to DSLRs and mirrorless cameras, iPhones have absolutely tiny sensors, and that isn’t going to change this year.

Given the same size sensor and a very slightly wider aperture, physics would suggest that we shouldn’t expect very much. 

The potential good news

There may be some reason for hope despite this. Including a mechanically variable aperture into one of the iPhone cameras is not a trivial task. It’s both complex and relatively expensive precisely because the lenses are so small. 

The question we have to ask, then, is why Apple would go to this trouble and expense for what we would expect to be a very marginal benefit? If it only delivers the kind of difference we would expect from the calculations alone, then it really doesn’t seem worthwhile.

That leads me to suspect that – if Apple really is going to make a marketing point of this new feature – then the company must have something up its sleeve. 

One possibility that strikes me is that the optical upgrade may be used almost as cover for a significant improvement to Portrait mode. While the simulated effect has grown better and better every year, there is still room for improvement, and perhaps the AI power of the upgraded chip has enabled Apple to produce something significantly more natural-looking?

If so, I doubt many people will care that it would be something of a cheat – the variable aperture providing a marginal benefit while the software delivers a far more meaningful one. What’s going to count for most people is the end result. This, then, is my best guess so far.

Do you have a better theory? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

title: Pixel 11 series getting early September update, not Android 17 QPR1
snippet: We’re expecting the stable release of Android 17 QPR1 in September. Before that, Google is rolling out an out-of-cycle update to the Pixel 11 series with a September 2026 security patch. more…
fullText:
We’re expecting the stable release of Android 17 QPR1 in September. Before that, Google is rolling out an out-of-cycle update to the Pixel 11 series with a September 2026 security patch.

On Tuesday afternoon, Pixel 11 series users received an OTA update to CD1A.260905.001.A1 (from CD1A.260714.001.A9). 

The Android security update level is “September 1, 2026.” (Note: Not September 5.) The install screen has the usual generic security message: “This update fixes critical bugs and improves the performance and stability of your device.”

So far, we have reports of an under 100 MB OTA hitting the Pixel 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold. Google has yet to post factory or OTA images as of Tuesday afternoon.

	

This is not Android 17 QPR1. Several of the visual changes coming in that release are not yet present, so this is still the initial release of Android 17.

Rather, Google is likely rolling out this update as a hot patch for Pixel 11 issues discovered since last month’s launch. The fact Google did not wait for Android 17 QPR1 should be telling.

title: macOS 27 developer beta 8 now available, here’s what’s coming
snippet: Continuing Apple’s weekly test releases ahead of the official launch of macOS 27 Golden Gate, the company is now rolling out beta 8 for developers. Here’s what to expect. Update 5:04 p.m. ET: Now available for public beta testers as well. more…
fullText:
Continuing Apple’s weekly test releases ahead of the official launch of macOS 27 Golden Gate, the company is now rolling out beta 8 for developers. Here’s what to expect.

Update 5:04 p.m. ET: Now available for public beta testers as well.  

macOS 27 beta 8 now available

Developers can now install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 8, continuing Apple’s work towards the operating system’s official release in a few weeks.

While macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 7 didn’t include any notable user-facing changes, beta 6 introduced redesigned traffic light window controls with a more Liquid Glass-like appearance.

At this stage of the beta cycle, Apple appears to be increasingly focused on bug fixes, performance improvements, and other under-the-hood changes ahead of macOS 27’s public release.

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces the new Siri app alongside Apple’s revamped Siri AI, as well as an AI-powered Shortcuts app that can create shortcuts from natural-language prompts. Safari also gains a prompt-based extension builder.

The update additionally includes new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, while restoring fixed-radius corners for windows and apps after macOS 26 introduced dynamically changing corner radii.

We’re digging through macOS 27 Golden beta 8 and will report back if we find anything new.

Installing the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here’s how to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 8:

Back up your Mac

Open System Settings

Go to General ⇾ Software Update

Click the ‘i’ icon next to Beta Updates

From the dropdown menu in the top-right, select the macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta

Hit ‘Done’

title: Google Maps has renamed ‘Lake America’ for users in the US
snippet: Following an executive order late last week, Google Maps has updated its label for “Lake Ontario” to “Lake America.” more…
fullText:
Following an executive order late last week, Google Maps has updated its label for “Lake Ontario” to “Lake America.”

If you are located within the United States, viewing “Lake Ontario” via Google Maps will now show the name “Lake America,” following last week’s executive order. 

Google, in a brief blog post, confirms that users in Canada will continue to see only “Lake Ontario” while users in other parts of the world will see “Lake Ontario (Lake America).” This can also be seen using a VPN.

From the United States
From Canada

Google continues to cite a policy in which it updates location names based on local government data; in this case, the US GNIS, where the name has been updated as of August 27 by the Department of the Interior following Trump’s order. Google referred to this same policy in February 2025 when it updated Maps to show “Gulf of America.”

	
	

Canada has confirmed that it will not be updating the name from “Lake Ontario,” with Prime Minister Mark Carney stating that “the name is more than 400 years ​old, predating ​both the Confederation of Canada ‌and ⁠the Declaration of Independence of the United States of ​America.” Carney added that the name comes “from the Wendat word Ontari’io, which, appropriately, means ‘the lake is beautiful, the lake is big.'”

Notably, competitor MapQuest has directly said it will not change the name, instead building out a name generator that allows users to create their own new names for the lake, mocking the change. Apple Maps is not yet showing the name either. Apple changed “Gulf of America” within a day or two of Google back in February, though.

Steep backlash pushed Google to limit new reviews of “Gulf of America” in 2025, but the same limitation has yet to be placed on “Lake America,” we observed in testing.

title: AirPods 5: Here’s what rumors say will launch next week
snippet: Rumors indicate AirPods 5 are launching next week alongside iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and iPhone Ultra. Here’s what we know so far about the new AirPods. more…
fullText:
Rumors indicate AirPods 5 are launching next week alongside iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and iPhone Ultra. Here’s what we know so far about the new AirPods.

AirPods 5 expected to launch at September 9 event in two models, but no cameras

Apple’s biggest event of the year is happening next week on September 9. Alongside new iPhones, Apple Watch models, and likely Home products, AirPods 5 are also expected to debut. 

AirPods 4 launched in 2024, and historically Apple has had two- or three-year gaps between generations. AirPods launched in 2016, AirPods 2 in 2019, AirPods 3 in 2021, and AirPods 4 in 2024. So from a timing standpoint, a launch this year more or less fits the pattern.

What’s surprising about the new AirPods, however, is how few rumors and leaks there have been about them.

Most AirPods rumors of late have centered on new models with cameras. A recent video leaked in Apple software showed the camera-equipped model in action, sparking speculation it would launch soon.

However, Mark Gurman at Bloomberg says AirPods with cameras will not arrive until 2027. But he’s expecting AirPods 5—without cameras—to debut at Apple’s September event. He recently wrote:

[Apple is] planning to debut fresh AirPods as early as the September product launch event. The rollout will include new AirPods 5, an update to Apple’s entry-level earbuds, the people said. That model was last refreshed in 2024. A camera-equipped version of the AirPods, meanwhile, isn’t expected until next year.

In a post on X, Gurman added that AirPods 5 will come in two distinct models:

with Active Noise Cancellation

without ANC

Previously in his reporting, Gurman wrote that he doesn’t anticipate AirPods 5 getting the heart-rate sensor from AirPods Pro 3, but Apple “is looking to add several more health features to the AirPods over time, including a temperature reader.” He also noted separately that Apple is “working on an H3 chip designed for less lag time and better audio quality.”

It’s unclear whether AirPods 5 will get the H3 chip or not. When Apple launched H2, it was exclusive to the AirPods Pro line initially.

But new health sensors are possible for AirPods 5, and H3 is a possibility too. Otherwise, details on AirPods 5 are minimal at this point. Perhaps like it did with AirPods Max 2 earlier this year, Apple will be able to surprise us with its AirPods 5 reveal.

title: Oura files to go public
snippet: The ring maker says that its business has shown significant revenue growth over the past year.
fullText:
Oura, the smart ring maker, has filed to go public. 

The filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday shows that Oura’s revenue has jumped substantially in the past year. The company went from $697 million in revenue during the nine-month period that ended June 30 last year to $1.2 billion during the corresponding period this year.

The company has said previously that it generated $500 million in revenue in 2024, roughly $1 billion in 2025, and that it expected to generate close to $2 billion in revenue this year.

The company says it has sold 3.6 million rings over the past year, and that it currently has approximately 5 million paid members — that is, users who subscribe to its service for broader health metrics. The filing also says that Oura has an approximately 85% weighted-average 12-month membership retention rate, meaning that roughly 85% of members who sign up in a given month are still subscribed a year later.

The company’s rings, which sell in the range of $350 to $400, are, at their most fundamental level, fitness trackers designed to measure a user’s biometrics — everything from metabolism and heart rate to stress levels and sleep patterns. Paired with an app, the ring and that software are marketed by Oura as an “always-on health intelligence platform.” 

Late last month, it was reported that Oura was looking to raise $3 billion during its expected public offering. The company, which was founded in Finland in 2013, confidentially filed for an IPO in May. Bloomberg previously reported that the company is expected to seek a $16 billion valuation. In October of last year, it had been valued at around $11 billion.

In its SEC filing, Oura outlines where it believes its audience can widen in the coming years. “We believe our opportunity extends beyond traditional wearable use cases centered on activity and fitness tracking,” it says. “We believe our platform can support significantly larger populations as we continue to expand access, build clinical evidence, and deepen integrations with health plans, employers, and care providers.”

Oura also notes how its trove of data is fueling new AI integrations. “We believe we have amassed one of the largest and highest-quality longitudinal biometric datasets in consumer health, tracking over 50 health and wellness metrics and representing nearly 42 billion hours of physiological data,” it states. “This dataset powers our AI and machine-learning models, which decode complex physiological patterns and improve in accuracy, personalization, and predictive capability as member histories deepen.”

TechCrunch has reached out to Oura for more information.

The company, which now has offices throughout the world, including San Francisco, was recently hit with a proposed class action lawsuit accusing it of misleading users about the accuracy of its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit alleges Oura’s rings can’t actually detect the physiological signals needed to determine sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that the complaint describes as little more reliable than a coin flip. The litigation follows years of online complaints from users who said that Oura consistently rated their sleep as optimal when, in fact, it was not. 

The company has disputed the allegations and previously told TechCrunch it will “defend against” the claims in the “appropriate legal forum.”

title: ‘Look up’ app for Googlebooks appears on Play Store, currently works on phones
snippet: Following Magic Pointer and Desktop Camera, Google has now released a “Look up” app for Googlebooks. more…
fullText:
Following Magic Pointer and Desktop Camera, Google has now released a “Look up” app for Googlebooks. 

Look up lets you “highlight a concept you want to explore, a new word, a trip destination, and more.” This opens a floating window, with screenshots showing a dictionary, flight tracker, “Overview,” and translator. The “Ask a follow-up question” field at the bottom provides a conversational Gemini experience. The Play Store icon is a pair of glasses badged by the Gemini spark.

Google explains that “Look up will use publicly available information from the relevant Google service (e.g. Search, Maps, Flights) to provide the best response in a helpful format.”

The desktop interface and package name — com.google.android.desktop.contextualtools — make it clear that this is for Googlebooks, though the app can be installed on phones as of today. 

	

When you highlight text, “Look up” will appear as a menu option. This brings up the floating panel with results. Google will presumably close this unintended availability on phones in short order.

Look up is roughly analogous to a similarly named macOS feature (“Look Up”) when you right-click.

title: The Best of IFA 2026: An Instant Pot for Cats, Camera-Equipped Toothbrush and More
snippet: The IFA 2026 tech event has begun, and these are the coolest devices we’ve spotted at the expo.
fullText:
CNET staffers have touched down in Berlin and are on the floor at IFA 2026, one of the world’s largest tech events where the future is on full display. From a camera-equipped dishwasher and toothbrush to Dyson’s largest air purifier and a speaker designed to soothe you to sleep, we’ve laid eyes on devices that could change how we live, breathe, clean, sleep, work and play. 

If you, too, would like to peer into the future and see what’s ahead, this is the best tech we’ve spotted at IFA 2026.

An all-seeing dishwasher

Miele’s Diamond G8 isn’t your average dishwasher.David Watsky/CNET

Miele’s new Diamond G8 dishwasher has an AI-powered internal camera that scans your dishes and decides how to wash them so it doesn’t miss a single spot. Though Home and Kitchen Managing Editor David Watsky, who saw the dishwasher in person, was skeptical about this feature, he was left impressed. 

But the Diamond G8’s scrubbing smarts don’t stop there. If you want the Diamond G8 to run only when electricity is most affordable, it can do that, too, waiting for the hours when power costs less. 

Note-taking earbuds

Plaud One: your AI note-taking assistant earbuds. Plaud/CNET

Going beyond its AI note-taking wearable pin and credit card-like device that you can attach to your phone, Plaud launched the Plaud One earbuds to capture and transcribe your conversations and calls. You can even talk to Plaud’s AI by saying, “Hey Plaud,” and then ask it your questions or give it directives. 

“We’d always recommend informing people that you’re using a recording device, and it’s important to note that recording phone calls without permission from all participants can be illegal in some states,” principal writer Katie Collins wrote when covering the Plaud One announcement. 

A robot vacuum that seals itself to carpet

The Roomba Max 875 Combo is all about clean carpet.iRobot

While robot vacuums are great for taking the effort out of keeping your floors clean, CNET’s testing has found that they don’t offer the same suction power as traditional vacuums. iRobot aims to improve on that with its new Roomba Max 875 Combo, which uses SealForce technology to seal itself to carpet and better suction up spots that need extra cleaning. 

In a video call with Home and Robotics Editor Ajay Kumar prior to IFA 2026, Adam Pope, vice president and chief engineer at iRobot, said SealForce is like pressing harder with a traditional vacuum to thoroughly clean a specific patch of carpet, but in a robot vacuum format. 

A smart ring puts contactless payments at your fingertips

Imagine how cool it will feel to use your ring for contactless payments.Circular

In addition to having the health-tracking capabilities we expect of smart rings, Circular has added contactless payments, a feature typically found on smartwatches and smartphones, to its new subscription-free Ring 3 Pro and Ring 3 Slim. When covering the launch, principal writer Vanessa Hand Orellana wrote that the company also gave both rings haptic vibration alerts, a feature previously available on its first Circular Ring, along with advanced sleep metrics, glucose trend estimates and access to its AI health coach.

A laptop built to be repaired

The Vero 16 comes with its own repair guide.Acer/CNET

With its new fourth-generation Vero 16, Acer brings the “right to repair” conversation into focus, as CNET writer Tyler Graham explained that the modular laptop is designed to let users easily upgrade its components themselves. There’s even a repair guide engraved on it to help with these swaps.

The Vero 16 didn’t come alone, as it was announced alongside Acer’s compact 14-inch Swift Blade 14 and sleek 16-inch Swift Air 16. 

A speaker that lulls you to sleep

Sleep has never sounded so sweet.Katie Collins/CNET

Alongside its Sleep Earbuds 4 and Sleep Earbuds 4 Pro with a touchscreen case, Anker introduced the SleepLab Pro speaker, which uses radar to track your sleep, breathing and heart rate, then customizes its audio to help you drift off to dreamland and stay there. “It looks like a thoughtfully designed piece of kit that I know I’d be happy to have on my bedside table,” Collins wrote when describing the device. It also triples as a sunrise alarm clock and a nightlight that glows in a range of shades. 

A non-Pro SleepLab has the same features, minus radar sleep tracking.  

Dyson’s largest air purifier

Air purifier or Dune sandworm? You decide.Dyson

The new Dyson HushJet Big+Quiet Cool Pure+Formaldehyde (try to say that five times fast) was designed to purify multiple rooms using the company’s most powerful processor. As Kumar put it, it looks like a Dune sandworm with its nozzle head that can be rotated and tilted. While operating quietly, the purifier can capture 99.99% of pollutants down to 0.01 microns for a breath of fresh air.

Lenovo’s first rollable work laptop

Lenovo is on a roll. Josh Goldman/CNET

Lenovo’s Project Swan concept is a laptop that expands horizontally at the touch of a button, transforming its display from 14 to 17 inches. But unlike the Legion Pro Rollable Graham spotted at CES 2026, this isn’t a gaming laptop – it’s for work. Perfect for work trips when you want a more compact 14-inch display for travel, but a 17-inch for getting the job done (or watching movies during your downtime). 

Dyson’s first toothbrush

Plaque begone!Tara Brown/CNET

Dubbed the CameraJet, Dyson’s first toothbrush has a built-in, AI-powered camera that detects gaps between your teeth within 100 milliseconds so that it can floss while you brush. To do so, the brush has an anti-gravity tank that its charging dock fills with mouthrinse, which its jet uses to floss. 

You can even use the CameraJet’s camera as an endoscope to see your teeth in the app, where brushing and flossing insights, coverage maps and guided cleaning are also available. However, this high-tech toothbrush comes at a cost: $500. 

An Instant Pot-like feeder for cats

Get your cat to stop meowing at you for food, and let them meow at this machine instead.David Watsky/CNET

Pet care and home cleaning company Neakasa showed off its Riko smart wet food maker, which Watsky described as an Instant Pot for cats. All you have to do is add water to Riko’s reservoir and freeze-dried food, so refrigeration isn’t required. On demand or when feeding time is scheduled in the app, the device will prepare your feline’s feast by rehydrating and mixing the cat food. Bon appetit!

A mom Roomba carrying its baby

One happy Roomba family. Ajay Kumar/CNET

Kumar, who covers robot vacuums for CNET and has seen all there is to see with these cleaning devices, was genuinely surprised when he set his sights on iRobot’s Roomba Duo. While it’s currently just a concept, the Duo has an egg-like mothership module with a floor washer and steamer and a mechanical arm that carries and deploys a slimmer baby Roomba to get under furniture and clean narrow spaces its larger mother module can’t reach. A true dynamic duo. 

A smart radiator valve

Its high-res screen shows temperature, settings and device status in real time.Sonoff

Home Security and Smart Home Senior Editor Tyler Lacoma has been waiting for a smart thermostat that isn’t just for forced air heating and cooling, and smart home company Sonoff displayed exactly that at IFA. The TRV Smart Thermostatic Radiator Valve provides three temperature scheduling plans and frost protection and anti-calcification reminders. It even connects to window sensors to prevent energy waste. Just screw it onto your radiator’s valve pipe and let it take care of the rest.

As IFA runs from Sept. 4 to Sept. 8, this is just the beginning. We’ll continue updating this list as we see the best that the tech event has to offer.

title: Android Auto tests Quick Settings and hilarious ‘Jimothy’ weather Easter egg [Gallery]
snippet: Google has some interesting tests going on behind the scenes of Android Auto right now, but only one of them is likely to actually be released – a new quick settings menu. more…
fullText:
Google has some interesting tests going on behind the scenes of Android Auto right now, but only one of them is likely to actually be released – a new quick settings menu.

About APK Insight: In this “APK Insight” post, we’ve decompiled the latest version of an application that Google uploaded to the Play Store. When we decompile these files (called APKs, in the case of Android apps), we’re able to see various lines of code within that hint at possible future features. Keep in mind that Google may or may not ever ship these features, and our interpretation of what they are may be imperfect. We’ll try to enable those that are closer to being finished, however, to show you how they’ll look in case that they do ship. With that in mind, read on.

In a teardown of Android Auto 17.6, we can see Google setting the stage for an implementation of Quick Settings tiles in the car UI. Strings currently point to a “Do Not Disturb” tile, but it lays the groundwork for future additions.

<string name=”quick_settings_tile_dnd”>Do Not Disturb</string>

<string name=”quick_settings_toast_dnd_off”>Do Not Disturb turned off</string>

<string name=”quick_settings_toast_dnd_on”>Do Not Disturb turned on</string>

This is not currently user-facing within Android Auto, but the folks over at Android Authority manually activated the feature, showing that it appears in the notification tray.

	

While this feels like a natural addition for Android Auto and like something Google would actually release to users, the other addition in Android Auto 17.6 feels like a fun little joke at best.

“Jimothy,” the viral raccoon, is hiding in Android Auto with a flag for a “Jimothy mode.”

SystemUi__jimothy_mode_enabled

Enabling this one shows “Jimothy” with weather animations, showing the current temperature and conditions on top of your music widget. It’s hilarious and very fun, but also incredibly unlikely to be something Google actually releases to the public – if nothing else, the meme’s time has passed. 

But, Google, this should absolutely happen with “Froggy,” as it’d be a fun and fitting way to finally show weather data consistently on Android Auto.

title: MacBook Neo 2: Here’s everything we know so far
snippet: Apple released the all-new MacBook Neo earlier this year, and it’s been a resounding success by all indications. Here’s everything we know so far about what’s next for Apple’s most affordable laptop … more…
fullText:
Apple released the all-new MacBook Neo earlier this year, and it’s been a resounding success by all indications. Here’s everything we know so far about what’s next for Apple’s most affordable laptop …

MacBook Neo 2 features

A19 Pro chip

The current MacBook Neo is powered by the A18 Pro chip, which is the same chip used in the iPhone 16 Pro. As reported by Bloomberg, Apple is working on a next-generation MacBook Neo powered by the A19 Pro chip.

In terms of performance, the A19 Pro is about 10-15% faster than the A18 Pro in single-core and multi-core CPU tests. The jump in GPU performance is even bigger, with benchmarks showing an up to 40% boost for the A19 Pro. This is because every GPU core in the A19 Pro has Neural Accelerators built in.

The A19 Pro chip is also used in the flagship iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone Air.

According to reporter Tim Culpan, Apple will likely use a “binned” version of the A19 Pro chip in the MacBook Neo. While the A19 Pro chip in the iPhone 17 Pro has a 6-core GPU, the MacBook Neo version of the chip will likely have a 5-core GPU.

More memory

One of the compromises of the MacBook Neo is that it has 8GB of RAM. The rest of Apple’s Mac lineup nowadays starts with 16GB of RAM.

The next-generation MacBook Neo won’t jump all the way to 16GB of RAM. Instead, it’s expected to offer 12GB of RAM thanks to the aforementioned A19 Pro.

As I wrote in my review, I don’t think it’s a huge limitation that the MacBook Neo has just 8GB of RAM. Still, an increase for the next-generation model is a great improvement.

New AI features

The combination of the A19 Pro chip and 12GB of RAM upgrades should also unlock support for Apple’s more powerful on-device AI model announced at WWDC. This model enables a more accurate dictation experience and new options for customizing the Siri voice.

The current MacBook Neo doesn’t support this feature because of its A18 Pro chip and 8GB of RAM.

New colors

The MacBook Neo is available in an array of fun colors, including citrus, blush, indigo, and silver. Bloomberg reports that Apple’s plan is to “periodically” update the MacBook Neo with new colors.

	

There aren’t any details on which colors the next-generation MacBook Neo will be available in.

MacBook Neo 2: Release date and wrap up

Apple released the current MacBook Neo in March. Tim Culpan reports that the A19 Pro version of the machine is slated for a release sometime in 2027.

What changes do you want Apple to make with the second-generation MacBook Neo? Are you a MacBook Neo user? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Xbox Cloud Gaming will limit players to 15 hours per month before they have to pay more
snippet: Microsoft is making a change to Xbox Cloud Gaming that will place a limit of 15 hours a month or less on players before they have to pay more for cloud gaming. more…
fullText:
Microsoft is making a change to Xbox Cloud Gaming that will place a limit of 15 hours a month or less on players before they have to pay more for cloud gaming.

In a post today, Microsoft details that Xbox Game Pass subscribers will now be limited to a set number of hours per month, a restriction that does not exist today. Limits depend on the Game Pass subscription tier, ranging from 5-15 hours per month.

Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours

Game Pass Premium: 10 hours

Game Pass Essential: 5 hours

Microsoft says that the change will impact “4% of Game Pass subscribers.”

Once someone uses up their allotted hours, more hours will be available for purchase through the Xbox Store. Pricing has not been announced, with more details to come in November when the change actually kicks in. Players will also be able to directly purchase cloud gaming hours even if they are not active Game Pass subscribers. 

	

Why the change? The company explains it is “because the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer,” presumably all the more so in the midst of RAMageddon.

title: Apple Watch loses a useful multitasking feature in watchOS 27 that I’ve been missing
snippet: I mentioned today in my Siri AI Apple Watch piece that there’s one change I still hope Apple makes to watchOS 27 before it ships this month. It’s one of those common muscle-memory features that have existed for years, and I’ve been missing it all summer. more…
fullText:
I mentioned today in my Siri AI Apple Watch piece that there’s one change I still hope Apple makes to watchOS 27 before it ships this month. It’s one of those common muscle-memory features that have existed for years, and I’ve been missing it all summer.

Double-clicking Digital Crown no longer quickly switches between apps in watchOS 27

As I wrote this morning:

Now my one watchOS 27 complaint is that double-clicking the Digital Crown no longer jumps between recent apps… maybe watchOS 27.1 will do something with the double-click gesture. For a device so button-constrained that only the Ultra gets an Action button, it’s odd to see a double-click gesture replaced with … nothing.

I also flagged the issue in July when Apple released the first watchOS 27 public beta version, and I shared the feedback with Apple in June as well.

For years, Apple Watch has included a hidden gesture type of feature for quickly switching between two apps, or the last used app and the watch face. 

It’s one of those behaviors that I haven’t thought about in years, but I’ve used it regularly.

Dynamic app grid appears for Digital Crown single- and double-click in watchOS 27

watchOS 27 beta 1 dropped the feature. The reason seems to be that Apple is really promoting the new “dynamic app grid” feature in watchOS 27. Clicking the Digital Crown now shows the Siri app icon, plus five intelligently suggested app icons, and the icon to view the full app grid. 

The dynamic app grid has grown on me over time. It’s great if the app you’re looking for is already in the suggested launcher. 

But it’s not a replacement for a sure-fire behavior like double-clicking to jump between apps. There’s just no way to do this anymore with watchOS 27. Double-clicking the Digital Crown in watchOS 27 beta does the same thing as single-clicking the button.

The old method was super quick for jumping between apps like Workout and Music and the like.

As I mentioned before, the Apple Watch is so button-limited that only the Ultra model has the Action button. With this in mind, I think it’s a mistake to remove a double-click gesture from one of those buttons. 

	

Double-clicking the side button below the Digital Crown still has its assignment: opening cards in Apple Wallet. Hopefully the final version of watchOS 27 restores the same gesture for the Digital Crown button, or at least watchOS 27.1.

Do you use this gesture on your Apple Watch? Is it something you’ve missed in watchOS 27 beta? Will you miss it when you update? Let us know in the comments.

title: We Rated the Weird Tech at IFA 2026 to Find the Wackiest Products
snippet: Tofu machines, pet phones, toothbrush cameras — we saw all the wildest stuff at IFA, and now we’re here to report back.
fullText:
We’ve been at Berlin’s massive IFA expo for the past few days, diving into all the latest the tech world is showing off. While we’ve seen deeply impressive plans for your home and computer, we’ve also seen things that just make us go, “…Huh.”

With so many innovations and approaches at IFA, some of it was bound to get weird. Out of the many robot vacuums, pool cleaners, foldable phones and headphones we found, we also kept track of the strangist things on the floor. Here’s what made us pause, what it’s supposed to do — and how useful we think it really is. 

Govee’s mood-reading skylight

Govee’s giant mood light was on display at IFA.David Watsky/CNET

Govee has long been at the forefront of strange home lighting creations, from literal curtains of light to spread across your garage to table lamps that look more like alien artifacts. Now Govee is showing off one of its oddest products yet: a dome-like ceiling light designed to mimic the sky and be “mood-responsive.”

In this case, mood-responsive means you can use Govee’s AI to talk about your mood or how you’re feeling, and the Govee app will suggest ceiling light color schemes to match. But the light can also create a specific blue wavelength designed to evoke blue skies and natural daylight.

Too weird to work? Not as weird as you may think. I’ve tested Govee’s AI before, and you really can generate lighting patterns based on your mood or random musings. But Govee already has so many lighting scenes in its app that I didn’t find it very practical — though definitely fun. I wonder how well it will work with a full ceiling light.

A gigantic tofu maker

The Nuvell plant protein maker is about the size of an espresso machine.David Watsky/CNET

If your two problems are not eating enough plant protein and having too much counter space, the Nuvell is here. This massive bean cooker and compressor is the size of an espresso machine and churns out blocks of tofu in as little as 30 minutes. It can make other vegan proteins depending on the legume you stick inside.

Plant protein made in the comfort of your kitchen.David Watsky/CNET

I asked the rep on duty whether the Nuvell could make cheese if you poured cow’s milk in. She claimed it could, but didn’t seem too confident.

Too weird to work? While it wasn’t operational at IFA, we assume the Nuvell does what it’s supposed to, since turning soybeans into tofu isn’t rocket science. The real question is whether it’s worth the space on your counter for this one-trick pony of a kitchen appliance.

A toothbrush with a built-in camera

A camera on your toothbrush is definitely a design choice.Dyson

Unless you’re a dentist, you probably don’t want a closer look at your teeth — but one intrepid brand came to IFA bearing a toothbrush that gets personal by using a built-in camera.

The Dyson Camerajet uses a camera with “Gap Optical Targeting.” Fortunately, you don’t have to personally review the 28 images per second the camera can take. Instead, an AI analyzes it for you and targets interdental gaps. From what we can tell, you can then aim the toothbrush’s jet of water at tooth gaps to make sure they get extra clean. 

If you do want to play dentist like this, it’ll cost a sweet $500 for the advance.

Too weird to work? I’m calling this one too weird for sure. Price aside, you have to stand with your toothbrush in hand while holding your phone in the other to look at an enormous close-up of your teeth on the screen, then simultaneously brush and use the water flosser at the right angles to hit what look like gaps. The whole thing appears entirely unnecessary if you simply practice good brushing and flossing.

A tiny robot vacuum… for your bed

Yep — a whole robot vacuum, just for the bed.Creatulize

Creatulize came to IFA to show off the smallest robot vacuum in all of Berlin. The X1 Pro is the brand’s second-gen bed robot vacuum, designed to clean your bedding and mattress. 

Using precision mode, the vac moves slowly and steadily across a mattress, sucking up dust, mites, hair and whatever else lurks. It can clean a king-size in about 20 minutes and has an easy-to-empty debris canister. Special sensors keep it from tumbling off the bed. When it hits an edge, it stops, turns and keeps on keepin’ on.

That’s one itty-bitty robot vac.David Watsky/CNET

Too weird to work? Mattress vacuums are becoming a thing, based on the idea that dirty mattresses exacerbate allergies. Nobody wants a dusty mattress, but whether or not you need a dedicated vacuum for it is up for debate. We’ll be testing the X1 Pro to find out.

An air conditioner trained to follow you

Midea’s new voice-controlled air conditioner follows you around the room with a stream of cool.David Watsky/CNET

One of the highlights we saw – and felt – was an air conditioner unit that sends custom cool air to you wherever you are. Midea’s new system uses spatial imaging and sensors to track your position in the room and deliver a stream of cool air your way. That means a cooler you and less energy wasted. 

Midea’s smart AC works with the brand’s other air-quality appliances, including the humidifier. The two work in harmony through Midea’s smart sync to keep your home’s air at your desired temperature and humidity, no matter what Mother Nature has planned. 

It’s also voice-activated, so you can turn it on or off, or activate the “mmWave sensor system” without getting up or even opening your phone.

Too weird to work? While the AC wasn’t officially up and running at IFA, Dyson launched a similar freestanding fan and air purifier that tracks humans in the room and spits fresh, cool air their way. We’re still testing that one in our lab, but would be surprised if the technology doesn’t live up to at least some of its promise.

SwitchBot’s AI shirt pin, the MindClip

SwitchBot’s AI clip sort of… spies on everyone around you.SwitchBot

If you thought AI was already in everything, just wait: SwitchBot is announcing the launch of its AI shirt device, the MindClip, at IFA. It’s made to clip onto your shirt pocket, collar, nearby strap or even belt. Once in place, it, well, essentially listens to everything that happens within a 3-meter radius for up to 20 hours and saves it for you.

The MindClip can recognize people by their voices and summarize conversations or events, ostensibly to help you with planning after a busy day. As far as AI goes, it’s no spying Meta glasses, but it is fairly invasive, especially for strangers you may be chatting with.  

Too weird to work? This isn’t the first time we’ve seen an AI pin, although it is the smallest and least distracting version I’ve spotted. The problem is that none of them really took off, and some companies even pivoted to an entirely different product. So yes, it’s too weird to work for now, but maybe the rumored AI capabilities in Apple’s AirPods will be an exception.

The AI-powered companion doll from Lovense

Lovense’s updated AI companion doll also made an appearance at IFA.Lovense

Singaporean intimacy and sex toy company Lovense has brought the latest version of its AI “companion doll” to IFA, aiming to make it more lifelike than ever before. In addition to talking, remembering past facts and adjusting its personality, the silicone doll can blink, smile and look when called by its custom name. Users can also chat with the doll at a distance via a phone app and set up roleplay scenarios, if they prefer.

Too weird to work? Yes, the age of AI sex dolls is here. But it’s such an eclectic — and expensive (between $4,000 and $8,000) — proposition, this one is only for those with very specific tastes and a, ahh, particular relationship with AI. For others, Lovense also debuted several more conventional, AI-free toys.

A Eufy sensor that asks if you fell down

Eufy’s new sensor has a very, very specific purpose in the home.Eufy

When today’s home sensors can do nearly anything from recognizing when dogs bark to knowing when someone is tampering with a mailbox, it may sound strange to make a sensor specifically to say, “Oops, it looks like you fell down!” But that’s just what Anker’s Eufy brand has done.

There’s method behind this madness. The wall sensor uses a combo of algorithms and presence sensing with mmWave technology, no cameras necessary. It’s made to help those aging in place or living in rest homes without creating privacy concerns. The sensor even supports two-way audio, so family members or nurses can check in if they get an alert about a potential fall.

Quick note: As Anker consolidates its brand names, Eufy products are staying with us, but the Eufy name may not be around forever, so keep that in mind when shopping.

Too weird to work? In this case, not at all. I’ve already seen mmWave technology tap into Wi-Fi signals to help those aging in place, although Eufy’s sensor is the first I’ve seen that focuses on falls and enables two-way audio for a quick checkup. It’s a strong use of the technology.

			

			

							
		

	

		

			Best DIY Home Security Systems of 2026: Install Them Yourself
		

					

Dodge installation fees and take security into your own hands with these super smart security kits.

						

		

A smartphone for your pet

The Petphone certainly makes a lot of claims about AI pet powers.Petpogo

Ucloudlink has brought the newest version of its award-winning PetPhone to IFA this year, showing a world where cats and dogs have their own smartphone, too. Sort of.

The Petpogo PetPhone is technically a smart pet collar, and we’ve reviewed many of those. But this version comes with two-way audio to talk to your pet with an app and AI features that interpret behavior and motion so pets can theoretically initiate a call themselves, as well as emotion analysis of barks, meows and other actions. It also supports more traditional capabilities like tracking and geofencing, and it alerts pet parents to out-of-routine behaviors.

Too weird to work? No AI features can accurately interpret specific barks or meows into moods and feelings. That’s (currently) nonsense. And trying to get your pet to “call” you with specific behaviors sounds dubious at best. So most of the innovations here are too weird, but the underlying collar functionality looks usable.

These headphones that turn into a Bluetooth speaker

TDM’s Bluetooth speaker headphone hybrid is confusing.TDM

TDM is showing off its unique Neo headphones, with a literal twist. In normal mode, they look like a typical pair of wireless headphones. But twist and collapse the earcups, and they form into a small Bluetooth speaker with up to 8 hours of music playback. The dual-device comes with an aux port, a USB-C charging port and a carrying case.

Too weird to work? When was the last time you saw someone with headphones and thought, “What a pleasant, private music experience that person is having, I wish there was a way for them to share it with all the people nearby?” Nope. No one likes it when you play music out loud in public spaces, especially when the same device could let you listen privately. I’m calling these headphones too weird to work.

A soundwave-creating smart bed

Amada’s acoustic mattress claims many different applications.Amada

Amada brought a fascinating mattress to IFA called the Soundwave Smart Mattress. Yes, it connects to a phone app. And yes, it really does produce sound waves or at least a “vibroacoustic experience” with vibration modes for presleep relaxation, meditation, focus and recharging. I’m not sure how vibration is supposed to help with those things, but CNET health expert Anna Gragert told me vibration therapy does have applications for recovery and disease treatment. The bed is made of polyurethane foam and polyester fabric, with a four-pin power connector.

Too weird to work? Well, Magic Fingers did have their day in hotel rooms across the US, but that day ended pretty fast. I don’t know if a bed with good vibrations is what the average home is looking for, but if you’ve tried it and it works for you, this could be a shakingly good upgrade.

Editor’s note: David Watsky’s travel costs for the IFA conference were covered by IFA. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own

											Tyler has worked on, lived with and tested all types of smart home and security technology for over a dozen years, explaining the latest features, privacy tricks, and top recommendations.
With degrees in Business Management, Literature and Technical Writing, Tyler takes every opportunity to play with the latest AI technology, push smart devices to their limits and occasionally throw cameras off his roof, all to find the best devices to trust in your life. He always checks with the renters (and pets) in his life to see what smart products can work for everyone, in every living situation. 
Living in beautiful Bend, Oregon gives Tyler plenty of opportunities to test the latest tech in every kind of weather and temperature. title: Google rolling out Gmail Live, Docs Live, and Keep Live
snippet: Following the announcement at I/O 2026, Google is rolling out Gmail Live, Docs Live, and Keep Live this week. After testing in recent months, these voice capabilities are now generally available. more…
fullText:
Following the announcement at I/O 2026, Google is rolling out Gmail Live, Docs Live, and Keep Live this week. After testing in recent months, these voice capabilities are now generally available.

Gmail Live lets you talk to your inbox. Instead of manually searching for information and reading through threads, Gemini lets you have a “natural, spoken conversation with your inbox to pull precise information.”

You can ask follow-up questions without repeating the context, and Gmail Live can be interrupted at any time to switch topics without starting a new session. The fullscreen interface shows a transcript and links to the source emails. To launch, tap the new Live icon in the Gmail search bar.

Gmail Live is available with Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra on Android and iOS in English worldwide.

	

Google positions Docs Live as a “hands-free thought partner and co-writer” that helps you quickly create a first draft for summaries, proposals, and more. Gemini can draw from information in your Gmail, Drive, Chat, and the web. 

It will show a recap of the information before proceeding to generate the document. You can ask Docs Live to add specific information and format as needed. In the Google Docs app, tapping the FAB (floating action button) reveals a new “Create with voice” option to launch the experience.

Docs Live is available with AI Pro and Ultra on Android and iOS.

Finally, Keep Live listens to “audio brain dumps and processes them” to generate notes and lists. Gemini “understands your stream of consciousness,” with Google Keep showing an inline preview of what it generated after a few seconds. 

You can tell Google Keep to put “ingredients for pesto pasta” in your shopping list, and “Gemini understands your intent and reflects it in the note.” Multiple notes can be generated in the same session, while you can use your voice to edit, like telling Keep Live to check off items.

Additionally, Keep Live isn’t limited to new notes and can add information to existing ones:

For example, if you already have a grocery list and you tell it you need to remember to get bananas, Keep will just add bananas to your existing list.

Keep Live is available on Android and requires AI Plus (updated), Pro, and Ultra. These three features are “coming soon” to Google Workspace business customers.

title: Judge blocks X rival from using Twitter name, but allows ‘Tweet’ for now
snippet: A federal judge temporarily barred an X rival from using the Twitter name, but found that X was likely to have abandoned the “Tweet” trademark and bird logo. The startup has since relaunched as Tweet.app.
fullText:
A federal court in Delaware has ruled on a trademark fight between Elon Musk’s X and a startup trying to launch a rival social network. The startup, Operation Bluebird, originally launched under the name Twitter.now, but the court barred it from using that name, siding with X on the core “Twitter” trademark. However, the court also found that X had likely abandoned two other, related trademarks: the word “tweet” and the Twitter bird logo, making them available to use. Operation Bluebird has since rebranded its website as Tweet.app, using the freed-up “tweet” name, and launched to the public.

The story of the Virginia-based startup isn’t really about building something unique; it’s about a company trying to get its hands on abandoned trademarks that X relinquished. Even the homepage for the company clearly states its purpose is to go back and pick up what Elon Musk dropped when he renamed the town square as X, and “threw the bird away on his way out,” it says.

The effort is headed up by two lawyers, including founder Michael Peroff, based in Illinois, and Stephen Coates, previously a trademark lawyer at Twitter. Given their legal backgrounds, their assertion that they’re interested in building a new social network seems dubious. It’s more likely they want to acquire Twitter’s trademarks, which have value of their own.

Still, Tweet.app is at least going through the motions and opening up to users in early testing. The company told TechCrunch that more than 172,000 people requested a handle on the site before launch. This was likely in large part due to the affinity people still have for the brand name “Twitter” — a name the company now can’t use.

Notably, the startup is charging users $20 to reserve their handle and join the social network, which likely helps cover its legal bills.

The court’s decision on the matter is not final, we should note. U.S. District Court Judge Colm F. Connolly issued a split ruling on X’s request for a preliminary injunction that sought to stop Operation Bluebird from using a series of Twitter trademarks that the startup says X had abandoned since its rebrand.

The judge granted X’s motion for a preliminary injunction regarding eight Twitter-related marks, but denied it when it came to the Tweet mark and the Twitter bird logo.

In the judge’s opinion, he wrote that Bluebird was “likely to succeed in proving both that X Corp. discontinued the bona fide use of the Tweet mark and Bird logo and that it intends not to resume the use of the marks.” 

The case will proceed to determine whether or not X ultimately still retains rights to any of the Twitter marks, given that the company now goes by X in most places. 

“They kept the word. They let go of the bird, and they let go of the tweet,” wrote Coates, who is president of Operation Bluebird, in an announcement about the rebrand shared via email with TechCrunch. “A tweet was never a corporation. It’s one person saying something. That word survived three years of a company trying to replace it, because the public declined to stop using it. We think that tells you who it belongs to,” he said.

title: The XGIMI Aura 3 lineup brings Google TV to 4K 120Hz capable short-throw laser projectors
snippet: XGIMI has officially unveiled its new ultra-short-throw (UST) projector lineup at IFA 2026 with the debut of the Aura 3 Series, consisting of the AURA 3 Pro and Aura 3 Max. more…
fullText:
XGIMI has officially unveiled its new ultra-short-throw (UST) projector lineup at IFA 2026 with the debut of the Aura 3 Series, consisting of the AURA 3 Pro and Aura 3 Max. 

Positioned as the world’s first 4K UST projectors to offer 4K 120Hz output, the series targets both high-end home theater setups and high-refresh-rate gaming on massive displays.

Both models in the Aura 3 lineup feature an RGB Triple Laser light engine paired with XGIMI’s Dynamic Dual Iris optical system. The dual-iris system regulates light output to achieve a native contrast ratio of up to 8,000:1 alongside Dynamic Black Enhancement. 

The top-tier Aura 3 Max delivers up to insane 5,700 ISO lumens of brightness and covers 110% of the BT.2020 color gamut. With an ultra-short throw ratio of 0.163:1, the projector can project a 120-inch picture when placed roughly eight inches away from a wall, with supported screen sizes reaching up to 200 inches. That’s more than big enough for any home entertainment system no matter where you’re planning on making a home theater upgrade.

	

HDR standards supported across the lineup include Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10, HLG, and IMAX Enhanced, along with Filmmaker Mode, dynamic tone mapping, and Anti-Rainbow Effect (Anti-RBE) technology. The system also includes support for 3D content – yes 3D content in the big ’26 – and even ships with two pairs of 3D glasses.

To handle 4K resolution at 120Hz, XGIMI uses two DLPC 8545 display controllers operating in parallel. This is really good news for gamers because high-frame-rate gaming features are enabled via HDMI 2.1 inputs, including Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM), AMD FreeSync Premium, and Dolby Vision Gaming, with claimed input latency dropping as low as 1ms depending on the mode.

On the software side, the Aura 3 Series runs Google TV out of the box and, unlike some options, provides native access to all the major streaming services such as Netflix, Prime Video, and YouTube, as well as Google Cast integration. Audio is handled by an integrated 80-watt Harman Kardon speaker setup supporting Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual:X. When the projector is idle, an “XGIMI WALL” ambient feature allows it to display curated wallpapers and digital art.

Pre-orders for the AURA 3 Series are open now on XGIMI’s official store. Buyers can reserve a unit ahead of time with a $50 / £50 deposit to lock in an additional $200 discount.

One of the only frustrations is that the lineup will officially launch via Kickstarter on October 20, 2026. Kickstarter exclusive pricing starts at $2,199 for the Aura 3 Pro and $2,399 for the flagship Aura 3 Max. Not cheap, but certainly one of the most space-conscious ways to refresh your home entertainment setup.

title: Apple reveals ‘shocking evidence’ from ex-employee’s MacBook in OpenAI suit
snippet: Apple has filed a new document in its ongoing lawsuit against OpenAI as it continues to push for expedited discovery. In today’s filing, Apple says that it has new “shocking evidence” based on early forensic inspection of a laptop used by former engineer Chang Liu. more…
fullText:
Apple has filed a new document in its ongoing lawsuit against OpenAI as it continues to push for expedited discovery. In today’s filing, Apple says that it has new “shocking evidence” based on early forensic inspection of a laptop used by former engineer Chang Liu.

Apple first filed the lawsuit in July, accusing ex-employees of stealing trade secrets for the benefit of OpenAI. It moved for a preliminary injunction a few weeks later, while also asking the court to expedite discovery, including early document production and depositions of key OpenAI employees and executives. Apple again emphasized the need for expedited discovery last week. OpenAI has called for dismissal. 

As covered before, Chang Liu is one of the parties named in Apple’s lawsuit. Liu was a senior system electrical engineer at Apple who left the company for OpenAI in January. The lawsuit alleges that Liu exploited a security bug to download confidential engineering files after leaving.

In today’s filing, Apple says that Liu’s lawyers recently handed over his MacBook that he used after leaving Apple. According to Apple, an “initial forensic analysis” of that MacBook revealed four things, quoted from Apple’s filing:

Mr. Liu not only downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic but also used it in his work at OpenAI;

Far from his unauthorized access to Apple’s third-party cloud storage being unknown to him, Mr. Liu and others at OpenAI were well-aware of that access;

Mr. Liu, upon learning of Apple’s internal investigation of him, sent instructions for destroying evidence to an OpenAI colleague who confirmed she would comply; and

Mr. Liu used a tool in his work at OpenAI that has the same name as an internal Apple engineering application used for Apple development work.

Apple alleges that Liu ran a simulation in March using the circuit schematic file in LTspice, an electrical engineering tool. In messages from around that time, Liu said his AI “agent” learned to run LTspice and review the results.

Apple argues that when trade secret information is fed into an AI agent or model that learns from it, that learning “may create irreversible and continually propagating uses of the trade secret.”

Apple says the defendants decided not to inspect the laptop and instead chose to “advance theories that the device’s data disproves.” 

Additionally, Apple learned about Liu’s use of the schematic because he used it on a Mac mini which later synced via iCloud to the MacBook he took from Apple. Apple now also wants access to that Mac mini. 

This “shocking evidence” is yet another point in favor of expedited discovery in the case, Apple says:

“This shocking evidence—which Defendants chose to ignore despite its availability—demonstrates why Apple urgently needs expedited discovery. The MacBook represents the very limited information Defendants provided so far (and only after weeks of delay), and shows Apple is not conducting ‘fishing expeditions’ but that its trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed.”

title: Narwal’s New Robot Vacuums and Floor Cleaners Are All About Better Mopping
snippet: Mops that can remove old and dried stains are everyone’s concern at IFA Berlin this year.
fullText:
Narwal has made some of the best robot vacuums and wet and dry mops we’ve tested here at CNET. Most recently, we were impressed by the Narwal Flow 2 and its impressive object avoidance and recognition, which earned it a spot on our best list. Narwhal’s new lineup, revealed at IFA Berlin 2026, features more models that continue to build on perfecting what works rather than revolutionary changes. 

The big news here is that Narwal’s FlowWash mopping, which used to be only on the flagship Flow series, is trickling its way down to other units in the lineup, like the Freo 20 and Freo 20 Edge. This is something we’ve seen happen across the industry. 

“For a decade, we’ve focused on making mopping truly effective in robotic cleaning. The Flow 2 represents the pinnacle of that journey, and with this new lineup, we’re bringing the expertise behind it to more homes while expanding into new cleaning categories,” Junbin Zhang, Founder and CEO of Narwal, said in a press statement.

Like other companies, Narwal considers mopping one of the biggest challenges for the robot vacuum industry, especially with the new focus on removing old, dried stains. Its FlowWash mopping system is one we’ve seen on other models, in which the mop roller is continuously refreshed and cleaned. 

Specifically with the FlowWash, the models include a microfiber flatted roller mop that the company says provides more consistent floor contact for stain removal. It also uses 16 angled water nozzles to refresh the mop with hot water during cleaning and an integrated scraper to remove dirt and wastewater. Finally, it has 12 newtons of downward pressure, which isn’t as high as some other robot vacuums we’ve seen at IFA, but it should get the job done, especially for models that shouldn’t cost as much. 

With the Freo 20, you get the mopping features, plus 31,000 pascals of suction power. There’s also improved navigation with dual RGB cameras and AI recognition of more than 300 household objects. Narwal says this model is designed for larger living spaces and more complex home environments.

With the Freo 20 Edge, you don’t get the more advanced AI object and clutter recognition, making it more suitable for apartments and less complicated spaces. However, it also has FlowWash, 31,000 pascals of suction, lidar, and structured light 3D navigation, a slim 9.5-centimeter body to get under furniture and a self-emptying and cleaning docking station. These are all higher-end features we used to see on flagships that are

Cordless and wet dry vacuums 

The Narwal V50 Cube is the company’s new cordless vacuum that comes with an auto-empty docking station, a feature that I loved on the Levoit Aero. The dock is compact and lightweight, while the V50 Cube still has 210 air watts of suction to handle pet hair and dirt. 

On the wet and dry cleaning side, Narwal has an Essential Model for daily cleaning and a Flagship Model with all the bells and whistles. The flagship model comes with 400-degree-Celsius steam and 95-degree-Celsius hot-water mopping, once again focused on stain removal and sterilization. It has 25,000 pascals of suction power, a floating scraper and a sensor that can detect dirt and adjust suction based on the floor conditions. It can lie flat and run for 40 minutes in AI mode. 

Price and availability 

The new models will start launching in European markets in September. The upcoming wet-and-dry vacuum range will also see new models in 2027, with launch details to follow.

In the US, the Narwal Freo 20 has been available on narwal.com and Amazon since Aug. 20 for $1,099, with a launch price of $900 until Thursday. The Narwal Freo 20 Edge is available starting Sept. 7 at narwal.com and on Amazon for $800, with a launch price of $700 from Sept. 7 to Sept. 20.

The US pricing and availability for the Narwal V50 Cube and the Narwal wet-and-dry vacuum will be determined later.

Editors’ note: Ajay Kumar’s travel costs for the IFA conference were covered by Roborock. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own

title: Chrome’s Android navigation bar redesign has too much chrome
snippet: I quite like how Chrome for Android’s main interface has essentially remained the same since 2012. The consistency is refreshing as everything else on my phone changes. While I’m open to modernization, the latest attempt at a redesign suffers from too much chrome. more…
fullText:
I quite like how Chrome for Android’s main interface has essentially remained the same since 2012. The consistency is refreshing as everything else on my phone changes. While I’m open to modernization, the latest attempt at a redesign suffers from too much chrome.

When the browser launched in 2008, the name was meant to signify speed and a minimal graphical user interface, or chrome. On Android, that philosophy has persisted with just an address bar at the top or bottom of the screen. That text field can be flanked by various buttons, but the most minimal state consists of just the tab switcher and three-dot overflow menu. Over the years, Google has just refreshed these elements while keeping the placement unchanged.

Old vs. new

The upcoming redesign once again adds a secondary toolbar at the bottom of the screen that has buttons for your homepage (which can be disabled), Gemini, new tab, and the tab switcher. This lets Google add a dedicated back button to the left of the Omnibox, while the toolbar shortcut is now placed inside.

	

Google was close to launching a similar revamp in 2020, but ultimately abandoned it because “mainstream users” found it “disorienting.”

I don’t mind the Gemini shortcut, and think giving people a dedicated new tab button is a good idea. That was my toolbar shortcut of choice for ages, and Google is now showing a share button by default next to the URL. (Tip: Long-press on the address bar to quickly copy links.)

If you keep the address bar at the top, this interface is perfectly fine. However, as a bottom bar user, the stacked interface elements are just so thick. When you first scroll down a page and the interface auto-hides, it really hammers home how much web content Chrome is covering.

Things become downright ridiculous when viewing Tab Groups. Having three rows stacked on top of one another looks comical and makes your screen feel infinitely smaller. To me, this interface is not usable, and I’ve forced myself back to the top address bar. 

Simply making the bottom toolbar thinner would help a great deal. It would salvage this redesign and let Google stick to the browser’s namesake design.

This navigation bar redesign is slowly rolling out to the stable channel. It’s not clear whether Google has committed to this interface, but I hope it changes before launch. Ideally, Google would preserve the original interface as an option, but that seems unlikely.

title: iPhone Ultra release timing: Here’s what the latest reporting says
snippet: Apple will unveil its foldable iPhone Ultra next week at the September event, but it’s unclear exactly when the new model will ship to users. Here’s what to expect per the latest reporting. more…
fullText:
Apple will unveil its foldable iPhone Ultra next week at the September event, but it’s unclear exactly when the new model will ship to users. Here’s what to expect per the latest reporting.

iPhone Ultra is likely to ship in September, but with very limited availability per reporting

Next week, Apple will debut its first ever foldable iPhone model: the iPhone Ultra. 

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are coming too, expected to go on sale later that week ahead of wide availability September 18.

But even though iPhone Ultra will be announced at the same event, it’s still unclear if Apple’s foldable model will actually ship to users at the same time as iPhone 18 Pro.

There have been countless reports over the last several months regarding the launch timing for iPhone Ultra. Fortunately, the most recent reporting is optimistic that we’ll see the device ship in September—albeit with limited supply.

Earlier this month, Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital said supply will be “extremely limited” at launch, but per his sources in the supply chain, there’s no evidence of a delay past September.

Similarly, a July report in Cailian News Agency referenced conversations with Apple supply chain sources. “They said that there was no change in the delivery time date in September, denying rumors of product postponement.” ChannelNews Australia was another recent source saying the device would be available in September, at least in the US.

Looking further back though, the story changes. 

Ming Chi-Kuo predicted earlier in the summer that iPhone Ultra will follow a similar strategy to the iPhone X in 2017. Meaning it could be announced in September but ship later in the fall. Macworld heard a similar plan from its sources.

And back in April, Nikkei Asia stirred a lot of buzz by reporting the foldable could be delayed several months into 2027. Mark Gurman at Bloomberg refuted that report though, saying the device was still “on track” for September.

iPhone Ultra release timing: wrap-up

In summary, the more recent reporting indicates that iPhone Ultra will indeed ship in September. It might be available in very limited territories and quantities, but early adopters should be able to buy it soon.

title: Leaker claims iPhone 18 Pro chip will have 7 GPU cores and faster RAM
snippet: A Chinese leaker with some track record has posted images of claimed circuit diagrams of the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models. These suggest that the new A20 Pro chip may have seven GPU cores – one more than its predecessor – and a faster memory interface … more…
fullText:
A Chinese leaker with some track record has posted images of claimed circuit diagrams of the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models.

These suggest that the new A20 Pro chip may have seven GPU cores – one more than its predecessor – and a faster memory interface … 

The images posted by Weibo user Fried White Rice are not of the A20 Pro chip itself, but rather diagrams of where the chip will be attached to the underlying circuit board. From this, they’re making inferences about the power and architecture of the new chip, drawing two main conclusions about likely improvements.

First, the diagrams point to six CPU cores in the same configuration as last year’s model: two high-performance ones and four efficiency cores. However, it appears that the cache memory for the efficiency cores has been increased.

We can see that the L2 cache for the small CPU cores has been increased—likely from 6 MB in the A19 Pro to 8 MB—while the L2 cache for the big CPU cores remains unchanged at 16 MB.

Trying to determine the number of GPU cores from the limited information provided by the solder diagrams is tricky, with six, seven and eight cores all possibilities. However, they conclude that seven cores is the most likely.

Again relying on the overall outline and solder‑ball positions, we can roughly deduce the GPU’s layout and explore several dozen configurations across three core counts—6, 7, and 8 cores. Ultimately, the 7‑core GPU configuration emerges as the most plausible arrangement.

Fixed Focus Digital recently suggested that the A20 Pro chip will be 18% faster than its predecessor with 30% better power efficiency.

9to5Mac’s Take

The Weibo account does have a certain amount of credibility, but this kind of indirect inference is very much a dark art. While the conclusions drawn are indeed plausible, they shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than informed guesses.
