title: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym
snippet: GymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it launched in 2017. Tap your watch to compatible gym equipment, and Apple Watch shares your heart rate while the machine sends back metrics like distance, incline, pace, and calories. With iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch. I tested the new GymKit on iPhone and AirPods Pro 3 experience with a GymKit-compatible treadmill. It basically gives you the Apple Watch GymKit workout tracking experience, just without the watch. This could be useful in a lot of scenarios. more…
fullText:
GymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it launched in 2017. Tap your watch to compatible gym equipment, and Apple Watch shares your heart rate while the machine sends back metrics like distance, incline, pace, and calories.

With iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch. I tested the new GymKit on iPhone and AirPods Pro 3 experience with a GymKit-compatible treadmill. It basically gives you the Apple Watch GymKit workout tracking experience, just without the watch. This could be useful in a lot of scenarios.

GymKit, no Apple Watch required

The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

As a side note: Apple Watch has more accurate treadmill workout tracking as part of watchOS 27. GymKit remains the gold standard for accurate data, though.

GymKit also avoids two awkward gym habits. You don’t need to hold the treadmill’s metal heart-rate contacts while jogging. You also do not need to wear a Bluetooth heart-rate strap.

AirPods Pro 3 become the heart-rate source (and likely your podcast or music audio source as well). iPhone becomes the workout computer, which you can monitor during your workout. And the treadmill fills in the machine data while providing the surface for walking or running.

iPhone and AirPods have become more like an Apple Watch

Apple has been moving more fitness features onto iPhone for years. iOS first made the Fitness app useful without Apple Watch as Apple Fitness+ leaned into iPhone as an entry point. AirPods Pro 3 pushed that further as the first AirPods with heart-rate tracking, after Apple tested the idea with Powerbeats Pro 2.

iOS 27 brings those pieces together. GymKit on iPhone shouldn’t replace Apple Watch for people who wear one every day. Instead, it’s a great backup when your Apple Watch is dead, charging, or left at home.

It also gives iPhone and AirPods users a taste of the Apple Watch experience, which could attract future Apple Watch customers.

In testing with iOS 27 beta 1, my Exercise ring didn’t update as I worked out without wearing Apple Watch. But after I put my watch back on, the Exercise ring caught up, and the workout appeared in Fitness with the right data.

My sample 16-minute treadmill walk showed 0.66 miles, 65 active calories, 97 total calories, 32 feet of elevation gain, and a 115 BPM average heart rate, just like if I’d worn an Apple Watch.

If I tried to use GymKit on iPhone without AirPods, the iPhone disconnected when the workout started because it had no heart-rate source. If I tried to start GymKit from iPhone while wearing Apple Watch, iOS pointed me back to the Workout app on Apple Watch instead, though you can continue without using the watch.

AirPods heart-rate permission also matters. You can manage it in Settings under your AirPods settings and privacy options. I had turned it off, mostly as a theoretical battery-saving move, but this test convinced me to turn it back on. AirPods Pro 3 can also work with Apple Watch to provide the best available heart-rate data.

GymKit on iPhone with AirPods is a great addition to Apple’s Fitness ecosystem

GymKit on iPhone is one of those iOS 27 features that sounds small until it solves a real problem. If Apple Watch is your default workout tracker, it probably stays that way.

But if your watch dies or you forget it at home, iPhone plus AirPods Pro 3 can now log a treadmill workout with real heart-rate data and real treadmill metrics. That’s a neat upgrade, and it makes Apple’s broader Fitness strategy feel more complete.

title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 is so popular that Samsung is stealing parts from next year’s phones just to make more
snippet: Samsung has a hit on its hands with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, to the point where the company is taking parts production from its 2027 smartphones just to meet demand for the foldable. more…
fullText:
Samsung has a hit on its hands with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, to the point where the company is taking parts production from its 2027 smartphones just to meet demand for the foldable.

ZDNet Korea reports that Samsung has run into a wall when it comes to boosting Galaxy Z Fold 8 production, with demand for the foldable far outpacing initial supply. Shipping delays were seen immediately after launch, and Samsung even set out to produce one million more units. 

The problem Samsung has run into, the report brings out, is around Display Driver ICs (DDIs). This specific part is built by a Taiwan-based semiconductor foundry, UMC, on a 22nm process with the partner having “reached its limit” around building these parts. As a result, Samsung is prioritizing DDI volume that was already secured for 2027 products and shifting that to boosting production of the Galaxy Z Fold 8.

Samsung isn’t directly using parts designed for other devices here, though, as the DDI is built specifically for each individual phone model. It’s the production of these parts that is being shifted around, which is still a major change on Samsung’s part. Samsung has also requested a “super hot run” – i.e. “express service” – for the Fold 8’s DDIs in order to meet demand. 

	

This comes as the Fold 8 is partially out of stock on Samsung.com in the US, and the foldable continues to contribute to a rapidly growing foldable market. Omdia this week reports that foldable shipments will double by 2028 to the tune of around 36 million units.

title: iOS 27 gives Apple Pay its best upgrade in years with redesign
snippet: iOS 27 introduces several improvements for Apple Pay, including a fully overhauled checkout flow that’s the service’s best upgrade in years. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 introduces several improvements for Apple Pay, including a fully overhauled checkout flow that’s the service’s best upgrade in years.

New design for Apple Pay checkout screen in iOS 27 is better in every way

Apple Pay checkout screen: new (left) vs old (right) 

Apple Pay has become one of the most popular payment methods in the world. It’s so universally available that even Walmart finally gave in and added support.

And with its popularity, any significant change Apple implements could be risky—especially a design change like iOS 27 brings.

Apple Pay has a new design in iOS 27 when checking out in apps or on the web. And I’m happy to report it’s a fantastic upgrade that’s better in every way.

The old checkout design had a couple main faults:

Switching cards wasn’t intuitive

Onscreen data wasn’t easy to parse at a glance

Despite years of using Apple Pay, I’ve still never gotten used to the historic method for switching cards. I always tap near the top where the active card is displayed, only to load the address screen and have to go back to find the actual card selection menu.

iOS 27 fixes that. When you first open the checkout interface, you’ll see additional cards on either side of your default card, indicating you can swipe between them to switch. It’s quick, easy, and far more intuitive.

Additionally, iOS 27 shows more information onscreen at once, and uses colorful icons to denote relevant info like shipping method and address, billing address, and more.

The redesign makes it much easier to verify everything is accurate and as it should be. Then you can quickly double click to pay with the assurance there are no mistakes.

Changing the design for something used by millions, and with real-world consequences for errors, is a tall task. But in my opinion, Apple has done a fantastic job with iOS 27’s Apple Pay revamp.

title: Gemini overlay gets bubble minimization and multitasking on Android
snippet: The Gemini overlay on Android now has a multitasking option that gives you a floating bubble shortcut when you Minimize. more…
fullText:
The Gemini overlay on Android now has a multitasking option that gives you a floating bubble shortcut when you Minimize.

The Gemini overlay now shows a “Minimize” button above the container. It’s centered immediately after you enter a prompt, while the pill-shaped container appears at the right after the response.

This collapses the overlay into a bubble with the spark logo. Google explains how: “Gemini is still available while you multitask. Tap to expand. Drag to move or dismiss.”

That said, the Gemini bubble is fixed to one of six positions and cannot be placed anywhere. Additionally, a bug appears to reset the bubble to the bottom-right corner after every minimization.

	

After the response has loaded, you can tap outside the sheet to get back the bubble. Using the system back gesture will close the entire overlay, while you can also drag to dismiss.

This shortcut is a bit faster than opening the Gemini app and then the side panel to return to a conversation. Another way to use it is asking a question and then minimizing to do something else instead of having to wait for the response. 

Alternatively, you could use Android 17’s system Bubble option with the Gemini app for a richer experience.

The Minimize button and Gemini bubble are widely rolling out on Android today.

title: New profile of John Ternus offers insight into life and reputation of Apple CEO
snippet: John Ternus became Apple’s new CEO this week, and today the Financial Times published a profile that offers fresh insights into Ternus’s life and reputation among Apple employees and partners. more…
fullText:
John Ternus became Apple’s new CEO this week, and today the Financial Times published a profile that offers fresh insights into Ternus’s life and reputation among Apple employees and partners.

Latest John Ternus profile has fresh details on Apple’s new CEO

John Ternus is Apple’s new CEO, stepping into the role just days ago as Tim Cook transitioned to Executive Chair.

9to5Mac Editor-in-Chief Chance Miller has a great rundown here of what we know about Ternus, including his education, early career, public statements, and more.

But a new profile published today at the Financial Times adds fresh details and insights to the story.

Regarding Ternus’s reputation inside Apple, it says he “is known within the company for being both highly competent and unshowy.” A key Apple supply partner echoes this:

“It was very obvious from the earliest days that John was super-talented,” says Wendell Weeks, chief executive of longtime Apple glass supplier Corning, who started working with him during the development of the iPad nearly two decades ago. Weeks describes Ternus as a humble “good guy” but adds that his hobby of racing cars might give an insight into another side of his character. “There are not many non-passionate people that drive race cars…but at the same time, you have to be wicked calm and really dedicated to excellence if you’re good at it. And John is good at it.”

One former Apple executive did tell FT that Ternus is “relatively unknown outside the hardware organisation” at the company. It’s unclear how recently that executive was at Apple, however, as Ternus’s presence internally seems to have been elevated in the past year.

Tim Cook has said that Apple “really wanted this transition to be the best.” And per one anecdote from the profile, it seems like it’s been received that way internally.

the company is celebrating what appears to be a smooth handover. A party for Ternus at Apple Park on Tuesday included DJing from Apple Music’s creative director Zane Lowe. But not everyone was there. One employee said they were already so acclimatised to the change in CEO that they did not feel the need to attend.

Beyond these insights, FT does add a few key tidbits about Ternus’s otherwise very private personal life. The profile says he is married, has children, and was born and raised in California.

title: IFA Finally Showed Me a Smart Answer for Home Radiator Heating
snippet: Sonoff arrived at IFA with a much-needed smart solution for radiators and I’m very happy.
fullText:
I’ve covered the many ways smart thermostats can convert your home to a well-heated haven and how quickly they can pay for themselves through energy savings, but there’s one glaring issue. Almost all smart thermostats are designed only for central hubs and forced air heating/cooling. Imagine my relief when Sonoff showed up at IFA 2026 with a smart alternative.

Read more: The Weirdest and Wackiest Tech We Found at IFA 2026

At last, I’ve found an alternative, thanks to Sonoff’s announcement of its latest TRV Smart Thermostatic Radiator Valve. It’s designed to fit on the valve pipe of a traditional home radiator, screwing in place and connecting to Wi-Fi to provide app insights and a full suite of control options. It’s available right now on the Sonoff website for $35 and supports both Celsius and Fahrenheit.

It’s difficult to find up-to-date smart radiator solutions in the IS, let alone everything Sonoff is offering here. The valve lets you adjust between several temperature plans and uses an IPS color screen to show temperature and settings at a glance. Its app also offers low-battery alerts so you can recharge it, as well as important reminders for frost protection, anti-calcification maintenance and even connections to window sensors that can automatically stop heating when windows are opened. There’s even a child lock to keep little fingers from messing up your heating schedule.

This combination of features is exactly what people need if they live in homes that primarily use radiators, have radiators in addition to central heating, or use radiators only in certain spots, like a finished basement. It offers the same savings potential and convenience as standard smart thermostats, plus some features tailored specifically for radiators.

Since I don’t have radiators in my home, I can’t easily test this smart valve out. I’ll have to ask other CNET editors if one of their rooms has a radiator they could test in so we can get real-world results, but everything looks promising here.

Are you more of a radiant floor heat home? Sonoff has you covered, too

Sonoff also has a smart upgrade for those with heated flooring. Sonoff

Many newer homes have a different kind of heating technology, radiant flooring heating, popular in bathrooms and homes with certain kinds of wood flooring. If you’re interested in smart additions to this kind of radiant heating, Sonoff brought good news to IFA for you, too. 

Sonoff also announced a Thermostat Core, designed to fit standard hydronic underfloor heating systems. It outfits floor heating with complete app controls, scheduling options and connection options with Sonoff temperature sensors, so floor heating can respond to the current temperature of a specific room. It sports a presence-activated screen, frost protection and other synergies similar to the radiator valve, too.

I don’t currently have pricing information for the Thermostat Core, but when I find out the details, I’ll let you know.

While I’m most excited about the smart heating, I’d be remiss not to mention that Sonoff announced several other smart products at IFA. It showed off an indoor siren and, most notably, a window security cam. Eufy also showed up with a window camera at IFA, so it’s apparently a new home security trend. Wyze got in the game much earlier this year with its own window security cam, and you can see what I thought about it here. These unique, covered cams fit directly on windows and are particularly useful for apartments and similar spots.

title: I Took the Pixel 11 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Around Delhi, and I Know Which Phone Camera’s the Best for Me
snippet: The Pixel 11 Pro debuted this summer with some new camera enhancements, and I wanted to see how it shapes up against the iPhone 17 Pro ahead of Apple’s Sept. 9 event.
fullText:
Google is promising “incredible camera upgrades” with its new $1,099 Pixel 11 Pro, but with a rumored iPhone 18 Pro likely debuting on Wednesday, I wanted to see how the phone’s photography shapes up against the iPhone 17 Pro. 

Google touts a few enhancements that could make a difference, including better dynamic range on its wide camera and 30% higher light sensitivity on its zoom sensor. And those boosts could improve photos, even if the 11 Pro’s camera hardware is largely similar to last year’s 10 Pro — featuring a 50-megapixel wide lens, a 48-megapixel ultrawide and a 48-megapixel telephoto with a 5x optical zoom.

Apple’s iPhone 17 Pro also has a mighty camera system even after a year on the market, with 48-megapixel wide, ultrawide and telephoto cameras. The telephoto camera has a 4x optical zoom that can achieve an 8x magnification with Apple’s software. 

Google Pixel 11 Pro’s camera system includes a 50-megapixel wide lens, a 48-megapixel ultrawide and a 48-megapixel telephoto with a 5x optical zoom.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

The two phones also offer their own versions of color profiles to help you add your creative style to the photos rather than relying on the default looks. However, for this comparison, I resorted to default processing across the lenses. Google tends to brighten the shadows, whereas Apple leans toward a more natural tone.

I took both phones around Delhi to see how they perform in a variety of environments, including a few beautiful monuments in Lodhi Garden that provided plenty of well-lit and shadowy areas to see how Apple and Google’s best phone cameras show these places off. While phone photography can vary in all kinds of environments and is subjective, here’s how I felt each phone performed in capturing fine details and colors.

Google Pixel 11 Pro

Apple iPhone 17 Pro

Main

50-megapixel; 1/1.3-inch sensor with OIS; 25mm

48-megapixel;1/1.28-inch sensor with OIS, 24mm

Telephoto

48-megapixel; 1/1.95-inch sensor with 5x optical zoom and OIS, 120mm

48-megapixel; 1/2.55-inch sensor with 4x optical zoom and OIS, 100mm

Ultrawide

48-megapixel; 123-degree field-of-view

48-megapixel; 120-degree field-of-view

Main camera

Left: Pixel 11 Pro image. Right: iPhone 17 Pro image.

In overcast conditions, Apple’s colors look more accurate to the scene, but the Pixel 11 Pro better exposed the overall frame. It delivered a better dynamic range, and if you look at the leaves on the trees, you’ll find that Google was able to capture more details in the shadows. The iPhone 17 Pro Max shot looks less lively in comparison.

Left: Pixel 11 Pro. Right: iPhone 17 Pro.

Both phones take decent portrait shots, but nothing like what you’d get from a Vivo, Xiaomi or Oppo’s Ultra models available in international markets. Those phones are still leagues ahead. In these shots, the Pixel 11 Pro has a pink-ish hue, but I still prefer it over the iPhone because my skin tone looks more natural here. The Apple portrait shot looks too processed for my taste. While these were shot on the main camera, Google is finally allowing Portraits to be taken using its telephoto camera.

Left: Pixel 11 Pro. Right: iPhone 17 Pro.

Both phones are capable of taking macro photos. The Pixel 11 Pro captured more textures on the flower petal while focusing on the water droplets. In comparison, the iPhone shot looks smoother, but I like Apple’s bokeh here. It looks more pleasant.

Left: Pixel 11 Pro. Right: iPhone 17 Pro.

I chose this frame because it transitions from dark to light and features a distant subject. The difference in colors is more apparent in 2x digital zoom. Apple leans on the warmer side, while Pixel has a comparatively cool color temperature. Both phones were able to capture a good amount of detail and retain the clarity at 1x.

Telephoto camera

The Pixel 11 Pro offers 5x optical zoom, whereas the iPhone 17 Pro offers 4x optical zoom. A black cat in a dark environment with backlight is one of the challenging scenes, but I couldn’t get the exact same frame because my furry friend decided to change its pose.

Left: Pixel 11 Pro at 5x zoom. Right: iPhone 17 Pro at 4x zoom.

The Pixel 11 Pro managed to capture more details and comparatively accurate colors. The cat’s yellow eyes are sharper on the Google phone, while you can also see the details on its fur. The iPhone, on the other hand, struggled with clarity — you do see the cat and the bricks, but I feel like the Pixel was able to make out more distinct details like the cat’s nose and the different shades of color on the building.

Left: Pixel 11 Pro at 5x zoom. Right: iPhone 17 Pro at 4x zoom.

I put my friend in a similar frame, and both phones captured the skin tone well but had some sort of halo effect — possibly from the light source behind my subject — that made the shot look unnatural. In terms of colors, the iPhone got my friend’s hair color right, while the Pixel’s cooler tone changed the shade of green.

Left: Pixel 11 Pro at 5x zoom. Right: iPhone 17 Pro at 4x zoom.

I prefer the Pixel 11 Pro shot in this comparison because of better contrast and more accurate skin tone. If you look at the building, you’ll notice that the iPhone 17 Pro photo is less sharp and doesn’t have the same amount of detail, including the texture in the green and pink parts of the monument. It is more pronounced in the Pixel shot.

Ultrawide camera

Left: Pixel 11 Pro ultrawide camera. Right: iPhone 17 Pro ultrawide camera.

In ultrawide angle too, the Pixel 11 Pro continues to better expose the shadows in darker areas of the photo. It is comparatively brighter, too, and I’d pick it over the iPhone shot. I’ve included the 1x shot here for context — the colors remain consistent across main and ultrawide cameras on both phones.

Left: Pixel 11 Pro at 1x zoom. Right: iPhone 17 Pro at 1x zoom.

The photography experience

For what I value in a photo, I preferred Google’s Pixel 11 Pro over Apple’s iPhone 17 Pro in most of the scenes I tested. I felt the Pixel 11 Pro’s photos had more contrast, brighter visuals, and I felt like it delivered sharper results in zoom shots. All of this equated to more lively, social media-ready shots.

I will caveat that I am not a fan of the Pixel 11 Pro’s camera app nor the Google Photos app — I find menu options like Camera Looks are buried in the viewfinder, and the Google Photos app puts too much emphasis on resurfacing throwback photos, especially when I’m in the middle of finding something different. It is cluttered and distracting.

	

			

Apple’s iPhone 17 Pro is still a very good option. I feel it offers a more accurate representation of the scenes I captured, even though I prefer the photos the Pixel 11 Pro created. I like how Google’s phone created brighter scenes, even if that was through more digital processing. 

As we look forward to the iPhone 18 Pro, I hope Apple’s next phone steps up its zoom photos — perhaps with a bigger telephoto sensor — to better compete against the zoomed photos I captured with the Pixel 11 Pro.

title: New iPhone Ultra details arrive for specs, multitasking, launch timing, more
snippet: Next week, the iPhone Ultra will be unveiled at Apple’s September event, and today a new Tom’s Guide interview with Mark Gurman reveals several fresh details on what to expect from specs, software, launch timing, and more. more…
fullText:
Next week, the iPhone Ultra will be unveiled at Apple’s September event, and today a new Tom’s Guide interview with Mark Gurman reveals several fresh details on what to expect from specs, software, launch timing, and more.

Here’s what’s coming with iPhone Ultra, per Mark Gurman

One week out from iPhone Ultra’s introduction, there are still new leaks arriving. Today in a new interview with Tom’s Guide, Mark Gurman shared a variety of tidbits—including some details not reported before.

MagSafe, for example, has been a recent question mark for iPhone Ultra. But Gurman was quick to say MagSafe won’t be absent. “MagSafe is there. Yeah, all indications that I’ve heard is that MagSafe is in for this foldable phone.”

When asked about specs for the iPhone Ultra, Gurman mentions:

5.5-inch cover display and 7.8-inch inner display

“Latest Apple Pro chip and latest Apple modem”

He also talks about two key features: the rumored “crease-less” display and liquid metal hinge. He says the crease isn’t entirely gone, but it’s comparable to the new Samsung foldables and might be even better thanks to the more durable hinge.

On the note of the hinge and durability, he adds:

The spec for Apple was to make the foldable phone as durable or at least close to it as any other iPhone. And that’s one of the things that they’ve spent a lot of time working on is the durability.

Multitasking was another key area addressed in the interview. Gurman previously reported that iOS 27 will enable iPad-like app layouts and side-by-side app multitasking. Today he adds that drag and drop will be supported between multiple on-screen apps, so you can quickly move data from one app to another.

Gurman also comments on launch timing, with encouraging news on that front:

I would be very surprised if the foldable phone did not come out at the same time as the new Pro phones, or very close to it. So either on the same launch date—a dual launch—or coming out within weeks later. This idea of a late October, a November launch, massive delays, supply chain issues, I don’t believe to be the case.

Finally, when asked about pricing, Gurman reiterates the same $2,000+ starting price expectation that he’s shared before.

You can watch the full interview below, which includes more details on what to expect from iPhone Ultra.

title: New Apple CEO John Ternus now has his own X account
snippet: The new Apple CEO has just launched their social media presence on X, with the handle @johnternus. His bio is simply ‘ CEO’, and his first post simply reads ‘hello’. Today is Ternus’s first official day in the top job, with outgoing Tim Cook moving to an Executive Chair role. more…
fullText:
The new Apple CEO has just launched their social media presence on X, with the handle @johnternus. His bio is simply ‘ CEO’, and his first post simply reads ‘hello’.

Today is Ternus’s first official day in the top job, with outgoing Tim Cook moving to an Executive Chair role.

Apple’s relationship with social media, in general, is intriguing. As a company, Apple maintains the @apple account on X, but does not post content other than running sponsored ads. However, executives like former CEO Tim Cook and SVP Marketing Greg Jozwiak do have public-facing profiles. 

We don’t know yet what kind of content Ternus will post on X, but we can assume it will be similar to how Cook’s account was managed. That includes posts announcing new products, and sporadic statements on various company initiatives. 

We can expect the Ternus account to be very busy come next Wednesday, when Apple hosts its big fall product announcement event including the launch of new iPhones and Apple Watches.

Ternus has risen to the CEO role following a five year stint as SVP of Hardware Engineering, and a twenty-five year career at Apple in general. He is seen as a more product-oriented CEO than the outgoing operations-mastermind Cook.

title: Sony’s new ULT Tower party speakers start at $450
snippet: Sony has announced new additions to its ULT Tower party speaker lineup, now offering options that are much more affordable. more…
fullText:
Sony has announced new additions to its ULT Tower party speaker lineup, now offering options that are much more affordable.

The Sony ULT Tower collection kicked off back in 2024 with a pricey but powerful $1,200 speaker. The ULT Tower 9 launched earlier this year with a smaller, but still pricey $900 package. These speakers are designed with parties in mind, delivering music on a much larger scale than a traditional Bluetooth speaker.

Now, Sony is expanding the lineup.

Three new Sony ULT Tower party speakers are launching in September, starting with the most affordable of the bunch, the ULT Tower 5. This is the most compact of the bunch – it’s not exactly small – but Sony says it still delivers “impressive bass and sound pressure.” Like the rest of the lineup, it also features four sound profiles, including: 

	

ULT1: Enhances deep bass for a rich, low-frequency sound that makes your heart tremble.

ULT2: Boosts even greater power, delivering body-shaking bass and strong sound pressure.

FLAT: Reproduces music exactly as intended, delivering a true-to-source listening experience.

LIVE: Recreates the spacious feel of a live performance while preserving vocal clarity.

ULT Tower 5 starts at $450, with the whole lineup on Sony’s website, Amazon, and more.

The whole lineup also supports wireless audio alongside XLR, USB, and Line inputs, as well as having a microphone input too. Multiple speakers can also be set up in a stereo pair.

Meanwhile, ULT Tower 7 offers more power and volume, as well as adding 360-degree audio at $650.

ULT Tower Max is the last option debuting this month, jumping up to the top of the lineup at $1,500. This monstrous party speaker has three woofers (two front and one back-facing) as well as four tweeters, 360-degree sound, and “a high-powered amplifier.”

title: Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe is a MacBook Neo competitor starting at $699
snippet: Lenovo is taking on the MacBook Neo with a colorful new laptop – the IdeaPad Vibe. more…
fullText:
Lenovo is taking on the MacBook Neo with a colorful new laptop – the IdeaPad Vibe.

Announced at Lenovo Innovation World ahead of IFA, the Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe is squarely aimed at Apple’s most affordable and incredibly popular MacBook Neo, and it puts up a good fight on paper. The laptop can be outfitted with either a 14-inch or 15-inch OLED display and measures in at 14.9mm thick and from 2.87lbs. Thicker and bigger than Apple’s laptop, but not all that much heavier, at least in its starting weight. Lenovo says the Vibe will be available in both plastic and metal variations.

Metal
Plastic

It sure looks the part, though, with Lenovo teaming up with Pantone to offer 7 different color options for the IdeaPad Vibe including:

Dreamy Violet: a muted violet shade layered with inviting depth that inspires serenity, bringing a sense of comfort wherever it goes.

Spicy Gold: A rich golden yellow that blends warmth and energy, creating a confident, welcoming feeling.

Zen Green: A nature inspired green hue that evokes a sense of balance, harmony, and encourages a slower pace.

Chill Blue: An icy blue with a crisp modern vibe that stimulates refreshing clarity and an effortless fresh start energy.

Radiant Coral: Warm and uplifting with an optimistic orange boost that brings friendliness and positivity wherever it goes.

Moody Blue: Expressing credibility and confidence, a deep blue hue conveying refined elegance.

Lowkey Grey: A timeless grey projecting strength, stability, and understated sophistication.

The keyboard also features interchangeable keycaps so you can customize the look with some fun color combinations.

	

These are all metal versions

Pretty colors only matter so much, though, and Lenovo has stacked this laptop with a pretty enticing setup. You get a pair of USB-A ports, an HDMI port, two USB-C ports, a headphone jack, and even a microSD card reader. There’s a 5MP webcam (with physical privacy cover), an optional keyboard backlight, and an optional touchscreen on the 15-inch size.

But what’s under the hood?

You can pick between an AMD Ryzen AI 400 chip or a Qualcomm Snapdragon X chip. The AMD model supports up to 32GB of RAM which can be upgraded by the end user. Configurations also include up to 1TB of storage, also upgradable and featuring dual slots. The Snapdragon version supports up to 24GB of RAM and, while the storage is still upgradable, the RAM is not. Lenovo says to also expect an Intel version in the future.

The Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe is launching in two initial waves. AMD models will be available in October, with Snapdragon to follow in November. Both will start at $699.99, matching the price of the MacBook Neo since Apple’s RAM-induced price hike. 

Meanwhile, Lenovo is also introducing the IdeaCentre AIO I which is an all-in-one desktop computer with a 24-inch or 27-inch display, similar colors to the Vibe, and a price starting at $939. It will also be available starting in November.

snippet: Brydge, the Apple accessory company that came back from the dead back in 2023, has just announced a new set of colour-matched keyboards for the entry-level iPad. fullText:
Brydge, the Apple accessory company that came back from the dead back in 2023, has just announced a new set of colour-matched keyboards for the entry-level iPad.

While Apple offers the iPad itself in a choice of four colours, the Magic Keyboard for it is only available in white. That’s what prompted Brydge to launch its latest lineup … 

The 11-inch base model iPad is available in a choice of silver, blue, pink, and yellow. Brydge is now offering what it describes as a premium aluminium keyboard to match each of the four colours.

The idea is simple: you chose your favorite iPad color. Now your keyboard can match it. Most aluminum iPad keyboards are offered in traditional neutral finishes. Brydge 11.0 takes a different approach, using color-matched anodized aluminum designed to match the iPad’s own Blue, Pink, Yellow and Silver finishes […] creating a setup that looks like it belongs together, rather than an iPad with a keyboard simply added on.

The company says that it offers the build quality and features Brydge products are known for. This includes  a solid aluminium construction, a full-size backlit keyboard with 1.3mm of travel, an all-glass multi-touch trackpad supporting all iPadOS gestures, and strong magnets to hold the iPad in place. Bluetooth automatically reconnects when the case is opened.

Battery life is said to be up to three months without the backlight and a total of 40 hours’ use with the backlight on. It is recharged via USB-C.

Known as the Brydge 11.0, the keyboard is compatible with the iPad (10th generation) and iPad (A16), and costs $159. This compares to $249 for Apple’s Magic Keyboard Folio. The lineup is set to go on sale on the company’s website and official Amazon store around the middle of the month.

title: When is Apple releasing new AirPods?
snippet: Apple’s AirPods lineup is stronger than ever, but there are already rumors about what’s coming next. Here’s everything we know so far about when Apple will release new AirPods. more…
fullText:
Apple’s AirPods lineup is stronger than ever, but there are already rumors about what’s coming next. Here’s everything we know so far about when Apple will release new AirPods.

Apple’s current AirPods lineup

Here is Apple’s AirPods lineup as it stands today:

AirPods 4 (currently on sale for $99)

AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation (currently on sale for $149)

AirPods Pro 3 (currently on sale for $99)

AirPods Max 2 (currently on sale for $479)

When is Apple releasing new AirPods? 

AirPods with cameras

The biggest change coming to Apple’s AirPods lineup is a new version of AirPods with built-in cameras.

This pair of AirPods will have a camera in both the left and the right earbuds. The cameras, however, aren’t designed for photo and video capture. Instead, they will be used in conjunction with Siri to provide context for the environment around you. Bloomberg has described them as “the eyes” for Siri.

For example, while looking at food ingredients, you could ask your AirPods what to make for dinner or for specific nutritional information. They might also integrate with other apps on your iPhone, such as Reminders and Maps, to provide environmental awareness features.

In terms of design, the AirPods with cameras will reportedly have longer stems than normal AirPods Pro to accommodate the cameras. There will also be a small LED light that automatically turns on when the cameras are capturing data.

The AirPods with cameras were originally slated for release in 2026. More recent reporting, however, suggests the timeline has slipped to late 2027 because of Apple Intelligence and Siri delays.

More on AirPods with cameras:

fullText:
Google morning. How many times have you written that before? I hope you had a lovely final weekend before Labor Day. This morning, I’m reading about tens of thousands of dollars’ worth of pristine Duck Hunt cartridges found in a box in Wisconsin, vigorously nodding my head along to John Oliver’s takedown of subscription bloat (but remember to subscribe to 9to5Google Pro anyway!), and wishing I had a 3D printer to create my dream storage and organization system.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

I think it’s safe to say that Google’s decision over the weekend to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America has been met with a bit of pushback.

	

In a blog post, Google says that it generally abides by the Geographic Names Information System when it comes to how it presents names on maps, and since Executive Order 14420 “directs the Board on Geographic Names (‘BGN’) to immediately rename Lake Ontario to Lake America and to update the Geographic Names Information System to appropriately reflect the change,” it was merely following its own protocols. Google went through the same rigmarole when it renamed Gulf of Mexico to Gulf of America in February 2025.

One beneficiary of the drama has been MapQuest, the company whose rise and subsequent fall can be directly traced to Google Maps’ ascent over the past two decades. In social media posts on Friday, the company showed a cropped map of Lake Ontario with the caption, “We’re not changing it,” inspiring widespread support alongside understandable questions of “MapQuest still exists?!”

Over the weekend, the company’s Android and iOS downloads shot up 128%, bringing it to the top of their respective “maps & navigation apps” categories on both platforms, and app usage was up 50x, according to owner System1. 

As of writing, Apple has yet to make the same change to its Maps app, but it’ll likely happen any day now, particularly because the President is applying pressure, according to reports. 

Though the name change itself amounts to a minor scuffle within the larger trade war between the US and Canada, Google Maps’ enormous reach — and companies’ reliance on its APIs — means that long after the heat has died down, its effects will be felt indefinitely.

✉️ Inbox

Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 rolling out with many Pixel bug fixes. Google’s relentless Android release cycle continues unabated, and Beta 4 appears more feature-filled than most.

Here’s everything new in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 [Gallery]

Android 17 QPR2 adds Status bar customization for notification, system icons

Google’s hyper-personalized ‘Dreambeans’ feed is now free to test. I’m still not sure exactly what Dreambeans is, but I know that it’s Google’s best new product name since Daydream.

Google made a cozy mobile game called ‘Froggy’s World’ & the whimsy is back. Just when you thought Froggy was going the way of the dodo, Google goes ahead and vibe-codes a Stardew Valley-like starring the titular amphibian. And who said Big Tech no longer has a sense of humor?

Google is making AI Overviews even bigger on some search queries. AI Overviews are becoming even harder to avoid, and it shows Google’s intent to keep people on Google, and not clicking away, as long as possible.

Gemini Notebook switching to compute-based usage limits, like Gemini app. Is the tool formerly known as NotebookLM so popular that Google needs to even further restrict its usage? I guess so.

Google announces ‘Expert Intelligence’ to let you add Play Books in Gemini Notebook. Gemini Notebook is becoming even more of a CliffsNotes competitor. Its new Expert Intelligence feature lets you embed participating books that you’ve purchased through Play Books into Gemini and treat them like a primary source. It’s an idea I’m curious to see authors either embrace or reject.

People are sticking the Fitbit Air to their bodies, literally, and it works [Gallery]. I kind of love this trend of seeing all the weird places people are sticking their Fitbit Airs (behave!). 

Google Nest lineup gets a price hike across nearly every camera & doorbell. The Google TV Streamer is getting a 50% price increase while Nest Cams and Doorbells are seeing hikes of between 11% and 33%. Not a great look for Google’s smart home platform.

🤝 Cc: David Imel

Welcome to a new project I’m calling Cc, where I ask interesting people in the community about what’s making them happy both inside and outside the world of tech. First up, my friend and long-time mobile journalist, David Imel.

What do you do for fun?

For fun I do landscape photography, host community events, hike, travel, play music and spend time with my friends. My most common hobby is walking. I love walking.

What is your relationship like with technology these days?

My relationship with technology is weird these days. I’ve been trying to do more things off-screen, like reading books and going to movies. I like hiking and walking because they get me off the internet. I feel that social media has been co-opted by oligarchs to make us hate each other; the more time I spend on social media, the worse I feel. Because of this, I’m trying to spend more time without any headphones in and without looking at screens, and it’s making me feel happier. I also do a lot of analog stuff like film photography and listening to records with my friends, because they feel more tangible.

What are three apps you can’t live without and why?

Pocket Casts. I’ve been using it for 16 years. It’s the longest app I’ve continuously used. I love it.

Viewfinder Preview and Second View. These are light meter and framing apps for my film photography. I use them all the time.

Moment Camera Pro II. I’ve been having a lot of fun taking photos on my phone and I shoot RAW through this app. It’s great.

What is a gadget that you love right now?

I’m loving the Fitbit Air. It’s nice to be able to use my analog watches but still get info about my health, especially since I’ve been taking my health more seriously this year.

What’s a recent book you loved?

I recently read both East of Eden and Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas.

East of Eden by John Steinbeck: This book is so well written. I love how wildly different the various characters are and the descriptions of Northern California.

Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas by Hunter S. Thompson: Just a wild fever dream of a book that is super fun and enjoyable to read.

What’s a recent album you loved?

The Place Behind the Stars by Streetlight Manifesto. Technically this album is only half out right now. It got delayed a few times and five of the songs are released so far. But this has been my favorite band since I discovered them in 2009 and new music from them is a blessing. The last album came out in 2013, so it’s been a long wait. The rest of the album is supposed to come out in mid-September. Currently, the album is called “Halfway to the Place Behind the Stars”.

Through This Fire Across From Peter Balkan by The Mountain Goats. This album came out last year and I love it. I was reminded of how much I loved it because The Mountain Goats just released a new album called “Days” and I did not like it much, but I listened to this one again and it is magical.

What’s a recent movie you loved?

Project Hail Mary because it was so lovely, especially in IMAX, but I also loved The Drama because of how divided it made people. And the performances were fantastic.

What’s something offline you do every day that brings you joy?

I go on very long walks every day. I usually average about 15,000 steps. I’ve also been bringing my guitar to the park almost every day and practicing it. But the #1 thing I’ve done every day since college is going to the local coffee shop every morning, catching up with the regulars and sipping some good coffee. I wake up early – usually around 7am, so it’s a really great little reprieve before the day starts.

Thank you, David, for being my guinea pig for this experiment.

➡️ FWD:

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

The FTC and 22 US States are suing Amazon (PDF) over “secretly and systematically overcharg[ing] its approximately 1.2 million advertising customers by manipulating the ‘auctions’ that it uses to set the price of ads on its platform.” In response, Amazon says that the FTC “fundamentally misunderstands how advertisers behave” and that “there is also no harm to consumers.”

Tim Cook’s last day as Apple CEO was August 31st. He penned an emotional letter to Apple employees: “I hope you know how much I appreciate you and what an honor it has been to be your CEO.” He says of incoming CEO John Ternus: “I take enormous comfort in handing the helm to someone as brilliant and wonderful and capable as John. Few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does.” (9to5Mac)

You’ve probably heard about the proliferation of Flock cameras being deployed around the US to track everything from individuals moving around a city to car license plates. You’ve also probably heard about the similarly swift backlash from community members who are tired of being followed, harassed, and, in some cases, wrongfully arrested. The NYTimes Daily podcast summarizes the whole dystopian affair.

A massive swath of Valve’s production Steam database from 2003 to 2013 has leaked, and with it comes a veritable treasure trove of unfinished game files, including from Portal 2, Left 4 Dead 2, and CS:GO. (Ars Technica)

The harness that started it all mere months ago, OpenClaw, is back with a massive 2.0 update. While it now has dozens of competitors, including Hermes Agent (which I prefer), it’s nice to see the OG getting a spit-shine.

title: Google made a cozy mobile game called ‘Froggy’s World’ & the whimsy is back
snippet: Google has quietly released a cozy mobile game called Froggy’s World in the vein of Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley. more…
fullText:
Google has quietly released a cozy mobile game called Froggy’s World in the vein of Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley.

Froggy’s World is accessed by searching “weather” on Google Search and tapping the new ‘play’ icon in the top-right corner of the Knowledge Panel card. 

There’s also a direct link here: share.google/refnf9gUiPMARpgJO. This game is only available on mobile and will not appear on desktop.

You help Google’s iconic Weather Frog spruce up their new home, which is the mushroom we’ve previously seen on the Nest Hub and other Smart Displays.

	

You pull weeds and collect tokens by tapping. The game explains how there are “different types of tokens based on the current weather”: day, night, rain, and snow. They can be exchanged for seeds and other decorative items (lamp posts, statues, etc.) that you plant to liven up your surroundings. This process will take a few days.

There are various characters that you can tap to see dialogue, while “Stash” — the recycling raccoon — is just adorable. 

The top left-corner notes your current temperature and wind conditions, as well as a token counter. The settings gear lets you switch Google Accounts (with progress saved between sessions), control the delightful background music, and sound effects. You can also reset your progress with “delete my data” at the bottom.

Game mechanics aside, Froggy’s World is hosted on dailygames.discover.google.com, which we first spotted in 2024.

Be sure to share what you find in the comments

title: How to run Mario Kart 64 with native Metal rendering, high frame rate, and HD textures on iPhone [Video]
snippet: Love Mario Kart 64 and want to play it on iPhone? You may have tried Delta or another N64 emulator in the past to make that happen. And while that works, it’s now possible to run the classic cart racer with native Metal rendering on iPhone. As we’ll discuss in this video and post, running Mario Kart 64 with native Metal rendering presents several key advantages over running the same game via an emulator. Combined with a Bluetooth controller like the Mocagen MC1, it’s the best way to play Nintendo’s classic cart racer on iPhone. more…
fullText:
Love Mario Kart 64 and want to play it on iPhone? You may have tried Delta or another N64 emulator in the past to make that happen. And while that works, it’s now possible to run the classic cart racer with native Metal rendering on iPhone. 

As we’ll discuss in this video and post, running Mario Kart 64 with native Metal rendering presents several key advantages over running the same game via an emulator. Combined with a Bluetooth controller like the Mocagen MC1, it’s the best way to play Nintendo’s classic cart racer on iPhone. 

Native vs emulation?

Libultraship is a library that provides a reimplementation of the original N64 SDK on today’s hardware. SpaghettiKart is a PC source port of the original decompiled Mario Kart 64 cartridge that leverages that library. Developer Chris Sotraidis then repackaged SpaghettiCart as a native iPhone app called SpaghettiPad that features native Metal rendering, Bluetooth controller support, enhanced visual capabilities, and more.

Video tutorial

Subscribe to 9to5Mac on YouTube for more videos

While it’s easier to get Mario Kart 64 running on iPhone via an emulator like Delta, running Mario Kart 64 natively on iPhone via SpaghettiPad provides a wide screen aspect ratio, frame rates up to 120 fps, higher resolution textures, better fps performance overall, plus lots of additional settings that aren’t available via emulation. And while SpaghettiPad isn’t devoid of glitches, I’ve noticed way less issues when compared to emulation.

One good example is Luigi Raceway, which features a jumbotron that mirrors your race activity. On the emulated version, the jumbotron is a choppy low frame rate mess, while it runs at a significantly higher locked-in fps on the native version. There a lots of little examples like this that I’ve noticed throughout my hands-on time.

Disclaimer: I own the original Mario Kart 64 cartridge. If you own the cartridge, you can dump the required ROM file. We will not be covering how to do that or how to download any ROMs.

How to run Mario Kart 64 natively on iPhone

Install iloader

Although iloader can be used to sideload an .ipa directly to your iPhone, the primary reason to use iloader for this tutorial is to use it as a way to facilitate the installation of SideStore. Beware of fake websites that try to charge money for this free open source software, you can visit the official website for iloader at iloader.app.

Step 1: Download iloader via GitHub.

Step 2: Mount the iloader.dmg and drag the iloader app to your Applications folder.

Step 3: Launch iloader and connect your iPhone to your Mac via USB. If prompted to trust the computer, do so and enter your device passcode.

Step 4: Click refresh under Device s, and you should see your iPhone listed.

Step 5: Enter your Apple ID Email and Password, and click Login. This Apple ID does not have to be associated with the account on your iPhone, and you do not have to be registered as an Apple Developer to do this. If you have two-factor authentication enabled, you’ll need to provide the authentication code that you receive from Apple.

Install SideStore

SideStore is an AltStore fork that lets you add repos, install .ipas, and signs and resigns those applications in the background to keep Apple’s 7-day development period from expiring. SideStore works in concert with LocalDevVPN to allow for truly wireless and Mac-free side-loaded app management.

Every app that you install with SideStore needs to register an App ID with Apple, and Apple limits non-developer logins to just 10 App IDs per week. After one week, these App IDs roll off. 

Apps installed via Side Store with non-developer logins are also limited to just three apps at once, and SideStore itself counts as one of those apps. 

Each app signing will expire after seven days, and you can refresh manually at any time. However, SideStore will automatically refresh apps in the background when connected to LocalDevVPN, and will re-register App IDs for installed apps automatically, no computer required. 

Step 6: Open iloader on your connected Mac, and click SideStore (Stable) under the Installers sections to install SideStore on your iPhone.

Step 7: On iPhone go to Settings → General → VPN & Device Management and tap the panel under Developer App that says “Not Trusted.” On the next page, tap Trust → Allow. 

Step 8: Open the SideStore on your iPhone, and you can select Don’t Allow on the network permission pop-up if desired, but you should choose to allow the notifications permission.

Install LocalDevVPN

LocalDevVPN is a free App Store app that serve as a loopback VPN that creates a virtual interface pointing back to your iPhone. It tricks iOS into thinking a paired Mac is attached to your iPhone, which provides the debug toolset that lets you install and refresh side loaded apps.

Step 9: On your iPhone go to the App Store and install LocalDevVPN. 

Step 10: Open LocalDevVPN, skip the welcome screen and click Connect → Allow. Enter your iPhone’s passcode to add a VPN configuration. The current status for LocalDevVPN should show Connected.

Install SpaghettiPad.ipa

Step 11: Download the SpaghettiPad.ipa from GitHub on your iPhone and save it to your iPhone’s download folder.

Step 12: Open SideStore, tap the My Apps tab at the bottom.

Step 13: From the My Apps tab, tap the + button in the upper left hand corner, and it will open the Files app interface. Select the SpaghettiPad.ipa and you will be prompted to sign in with your Apple ID on SideStore. You can use the same login/pass that you used for iloader.

Step 14: You should now see SpaghettiPad on your iPhone’s Home Screen.

Configure SpaghettiPad

Disclaimer: I own the original Mario Kart 64 cartridge. If you own the cartridge, you can dump the required ROM file. We will not be covering how to do that or how to download any ROMs.

Step 15: Via the files app, move the Mario Kart 64 (USA).z64 rom to On My iPhone → SpaghettiPad. 

Step 16: Open SpaghettiPad on iPhone, and tap Rescan on the “Add your game” pop-up. The next popup should say “Found Mario Kart 64 (US).” Tap the OK button to continue. You should see a black screen for a while, and then the “libultraship” splash screen will be displayed followed by the Mario Kart 64 title screen.

Step 17: Download the Mario Kart 64 HD texture pack and save the .o2r file to On My iPhone → SpaghettiPad → mods.

Step 18: Open SpaghettiPad and tap the ellipses button to open settings. Tap Enhancements → Texture Packs → Check Again. You should see a pop-up that says Texture pack detected. Tap OK. Tap the power button in the upper-right hand corner to quit SpaghettiPad, and the reopen SpaghettiPad to load the texture pack. 

Disable the libultraship splash screen

Step 19: Open SpaghettiPad settings again, and tap General. Under Startup Behavior, select Authentic. Now when you open SpaghettiPad, it will skip the libultraship splash screen. 

Enable higher Mario Kart 64 frame rates

Step 20: Open SpaghettiPad settings once more, and tap Graphics. Tap 60 FPS to jump directly to 60 FPS frame rate. If your device supports ProMotion, you can even select 120 FPS.

Connect a controller

There are many USB and Bluetooth controller options for gaming on the iPhone, including Nintendo’s own Switch Pro controllers, but I’ve really been enjoying the budget-friendly Mocagen MC1. It’s a spring-loaded controller that allows you to mount your iPhone inside and connect via Bluetooth. It features Hall effect analog sticks, USB-C charging, rumble support, dual triggers, RGB lighting, and more. In my hands-on experience it works very well with Mario Kart 64 on iPhone, and it features good build quality for the price.

9to5Mac’s Take

Emulating Mario Kart 64 via an app like Delta might be easier, but it doesn’t take that much effort to get SpaghettiPad running on an iPhone, and it provides a much better experience. SpaghettiPad provides full screen gameplay, higher resolution textures, and much higher frame rates than the emulated version of Mario Kart 64. If you’re looking for the best way to play this classic title on the go, this is the best way to do so.

title: MagSafe Monday: Anker’s foldable 3-in-1 charger brings 25-watt Qi2 charging into something pocket-sized
snippet: The dream for your Apple gear while traveling is one thing, not a collection of cables and wall adapters. There are plenty of options for that, but often they are bulky. Anker’s Prime Qi2 25W Foldable 3-in-1 Wireless Charger aims to address that. It folds flat, weighs about as much as an iPhone 17 Pro Max, and charges your iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods. more…
fullText:
The dream for your Apple gear while traveling is one thing, not a collection of cables and wall adapters. There are plenty of options for that, but often they are bulky. Anker’s Prime Qi2 25W Foldable 3-in-1 Wireless Charger aims to address that. It folds flat, weighs about as much as an iPhone 17 Pro Max, and charges your iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

A 3-in-1 that folds flat

The whole pitch for this product is right in the name: it’s palm-sized and folds flat to fit in a pocket, bag, or travel crossbody, so it doesn’t take up much space. I’ve packed plenty of MagSafe stands for trips before, and they almost always end up being the bulkiest thing in my laptop bag.

Qi2 25-watt speeds

This is Qi2.2 certified, so you’re getting up to 25 watts of MagSafe charging rather than the old 7.5W ceiling that most MagSafe accessories were stuck at for years. Anker says it can get an iPhone 17 Pro to 50% in 26 minutes, up to 5 times faster than a standard 5-watt wireless charger. Your results will vary depending on the iPhone and its temperature, but even landing somewhere in that neighborhood is plenty.

Faster MagSafe charging usually means more heat, so Anker built in what they call AirCool temperature control. It runs at 19 dB, which is quiet enough you won’t hear it working, and it’s designed to keep your phone under 98.6°F while still delivering full 25-watt charging. Heat is the enemy of long-term battery health and charging speeds, so if this actually holds up to that claim in daily use, it’s a meaningful feature, not just a marketing bullet point.

The 3-in-1 layout covers your iPhone on the main MagSafe puck, an MFi-certified Apple Watch charger on the side, and a charging pad at the base for your AirPods. That’s the whole value proposition of a station like this: one cable to a power outlet instead of three separate chargers and three separate cables crammed into a bag. Here’s what Anker includes in the box:

Anker Prime Wireless Charging Station

45-watt USB-C wall plug

5 ft USB-C to USB-C cable

I love that Anker includes the wall adapter in the box, which matters since many chargers in this category assume you already own a fast enough brick. It also supports 110V to 220V input, so it’s a great item  for international trips without needing a separate voltage converter. 

Wrap up

Anker has made plenty of 3-in-1 chargers over the years, but the folding design is what makes this one stand out amongst a crowded market. It solves the actual reason most people leave their charging stand at home when they travel: they just don’t pack well. This one does.

You can buy the Anker Prime Qi2 25-watt Foldable 3-in-1 Wireless Charger from Amazon or directly from Anker.

title: Apple Is Full of Surprises. Here’s What CNET Readers Anticipate Ahead of Wednesday’s Event
snippet: From three new iPhone models to a Cook-Ternus reunion, here’s what could go down.
fullText:
The third and final round of CNET’s Big Guessing Game is now closed, which completes our contest. We’ll be back after Apple’s “Surprise and shine” event on Wednesday, Sept. 9 to share the final answers and determine the winners 

The CNET Group’s Big Guessing Game contest was held across CNET, Lifehacker, Mashable, PCMag and ZDNET. There were three rounds of guessing to predict what Apple will unveil this year. Each correct answer earns one chance in a drawing to win the latest Apple Watch announced in this month. Before we get into your answers in the final round, here’s a recap of the first round and second round. 

Over 70% think Apple’s new and former CEOs will appear together

Most (71%) contest participants say we can expect Apple’s new CEO John Ternus and former CEO Tim Cook to appear together at the event. 

As of Sept. 1, Ternus is Apple’s new CEO after 15 years of Cook’s leadership, and Cook has become the company’s executive chairman. Ternus sent a memo to the Apple team thanking Cook and the Apple team for their work and expressing excitement for a “huge launch.” Have we ever seen two of Apple’s CEOs share the stage before? 

Cook’s predecessor, Steve Jobs, didn’t appear on stage with him at Apple’s September event in 2011. Ternus and Cook didn’t appear together at Apple’s WWDC event in June, the last before Cook stepped down, but that doesn’t mean we won’t see Ternus and Cook next week. 

Three new iPhone models are what readers expect 

Half of CNET’s respondents (50%) expect three new iPhone models next week. In round two, 80% of respondents guessed Apple’s first foldable phone would appear at the fall event. We could also see the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models make an appearance next Wednesday. Some analysts don’t expect to see a iPhone 18 base model this year. Apple could be doing a split launch where some additional models from the iPhone 18 series lineup are announced next week and others in 2027. 

Guesses indicate the new foldable iPhone could cost close to $2,000 

CNET readers’ guesses about the price of Apple’s foldable iPhone averaged $1,847, but analysts predict the phone will cost between $2,000 and $2,500. A TrendForce report says the foldable could cost even more, starting between $2,099 and $2,299 due to the RAM shortage and increase in hardware costs. 

How much people are willing to spend on a foldable iPhone is quite different. A recent CNET survey found that US adults interested in the phone are only willing to spend an average of $781, significantly less than the expected price. 

Most think a new Apple Watch Ultra 4 will be part of the fall lineup 

Close to 3 in 4 (74%) contestants expect Apple to release the Apple Watch Ultra 4 on Wednesday, while 26% don’t think it will happen. Bloomberg reports we can expect new health and fitness features in Apple’s new watch, plus a faster chip. However, the design will likely remain the same. There’s also a chance Apple could unveil the Apple Watch Series 12 with a familiar design and biometric authentication. 

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 and Apple Watch Series 11 were both released last September, but the Ultra 2 was released 2023, with no new model in 2024. 

Readers think a foldable iPhone will be Apple’s ‘One More Thing’ moment at Surprise and Shine 

Apple is full of surprises and could unveil new devices that we didn’t see coming. But CNET readers seem fairly certain that the foldable iPhone will be next week’s “One More Thing” moment.

The foldable iPhone (18%) is at the top of the list of potential surprise reveals. It’s closely followed by a new Home hub (14%), which could double as an AI-powered smart display hub that was expected earlier this year but was delayed due to Siri issues. 

Some CNET readers also suspect Apple could reveal new AirPods (10%), and others expect smart glasses (8%) will likely be unveiled until later in 2027 due to rumors of “bumps” in development next year. Some readers also predict a new Apple TV (7%), which could have an upgraded processor and Apple Intelligence.

Read and watch all of CNET’s Apple event coverage next week to learn if your guesses were correct.

title: Steve Jobs in 1996: ‘I still think Apple has a future’
snippet: Apple has a new CEO today. Meanwhile, a vintage video of Steve Jobs from 1996 has resurfaced. It adds some incredible perspective. more…
fullText:
Apple has a new CEO today. Meanwhile, a vintage video of Steve Jobs from 1996 has resurfaced. It adds some incredible perspective.

The interview is from Maryland Public Television’s Wall Street Week with Louis Rukeyser.

The interview took place before Jobs returned to Apple. It includes a remarkable comment about his belief that Apple could innovate its way out of demise.

“I think the way out is not to slash and burn. It’s to innovate. That’s how Apple got to its glory, and I think that’s how Apple could return to it.”

Three decades later, it worked out (for Apple, Pixar, and Toy Story).

H/T Patrick McGee

title: Phil Schiller steps down from leading the App Store and Apple events
snippet: Phil Schiller is stepping down from his role leading the App Store and Apple events, according to a new Bloomberg report. The move is the latest progression of Schiller’s tenure at Apple, which spans multiple decades. more…
fullText:
Phil Schiller is stepping down from his role leading the App Store and Apple events, according to a new Bloomberg report. The move is the latest progression of Schiller’s tenure at Apple, which spans multiple decades.

Phil Schiller will remain an ‘Apple Fellow’ for now

Schiller was Apple’s senior vice president of worldwide marketing until 2020, when he transitioned into a new “Apple Fellow” role. Greg Joswiak took over the SVP marketing role at that point.

When Apple announced Schiller’s transition to Apple Fellow, it said he would continue to lead the App Store and Apple events. In 2024, The Wall Street Journal reported that Schiller was still working “nearly 80 hours a week.”

Despite stepping down as head of the App Store and Apple events, Schiller will remain an Apple Fellow and work on “unspecified initiatives.” Still, the report says that Apple employees believe this is a “big step” toward Schiller eventually retiring.

In conjunction with Schiller’s departure, Bloomberg reports that Apple is shifting leadership of the App Store to its services team led by Eddy Cue.

With the latest change, Apple is moving responsibility for the App Store over to the services division run by executive Eddy Cue. He previously oversaw the App Store until 2015, when that job was given to Schiller and the marketing department. Cue is taking on a more influential role under Ternus, Bloomberg has reported.

On a day-to-day basis, the App Store will be led by Carson Oliver, a veteran of the department who is now reporting directly to Cue. Two years ago, Schiller split up responsibility for the App Store among two direct reports, Oliver and Ann Thai.

Leadership of Apple events, meanwhile, is being handed to Nola Weinstein, who “has led that function as Schiller’s deputy since 2023.” Weinstein will report to Kristin Huguet Quayle, Apple’s VP of communications and public relations.

The big news of the day, of course, is that today marks Tim Cook’s last day as Apple CEO. John Ternus will take the keys on Tuesday. Cook commemorated his last day as CEO in a memo to Apple employees, which you can read here.
